frames.text: Carl Clark hosted the Monday Niters, this past week.  And amid the usual curses and smart comments, I asked the fellas to use “f” words, when giving their predictions and comments. It just seemed like something to do.  So what follows is a host of “f” words, sprinkled throughout the narrative.  See how many you can spot. First off, the Chiefs are five and three, losing all three games on the road. But another fact is that they have won all three games and home plus one away game at Cleveland.  Most commentators, including our own, say the Chiefs are fading.  Well, that’s a bunch of flak.  Because this is the same team that everyone was raving fire about, just three weeks ago.  However discontented you may be, folk still believe the Chiefs are playoff-bound.  Losing to Oakland last week put them only a half game up on the Raiders.  And many say that San Diego is just beginning its usual, late-season rise.  But, don’t be moved by any of that crap. Chiefs still have fire-power and it will re-emerge against Denver on Sunday. If for no more than to save face.  Let’s now see what the guys say about the dreaded Denver game, in Denver. Dr. Charles “A Real Likeable Guy” Allen: Doc believes that the Chiefs will commit a felony against the Broncos.  Quietly but forcefully, he says the Broncos don’t have a team that can match with the Chiefs. Practising pain-free dentistry for thirty two years, Doc says the Chiefs will still win the West.  Chiefs by 14 Paul “That Hater” Booker: Most people like Booker.  He’s pleasant and he’s a good road buddy.  There is no joint in town that Booker has not inspected. But, he’s a Chiefs hater, laughingly saying that the Chiefs fantasy time is over.  That Booker just can’t see the light, when it comes to the Chiefs.  He predicted rightly last week and that fact gives rise to his fight to end this Chiefs’ mania. He has sealed the Chiefs fate.  Denver by 3 Carl “Mr. President” Clark: You know Carl is now President of the Ivanhoe Club.  Along with folk like Jon Gray, he is trying to make life better for this century-old club.  After thinking it over for four weeks now, he thinks Carl has made a transition to a loyalist and he’s got the fever. Chiefs by 7 Congressman “Faith-filled” Cleaver: As you know, Cleaver just beat out a fakir, in his quest to retain his seat in Congress.  He actually sat down and chilled a little with us, this last Monday. He ate his little fish and followed up his comments with a funky remarked, aimed at Coach Haley.  Though he won’t forget that Oakland fiasco, he still believes in the Chiefs. Chiefs by 10 Ike  “Idi Amin” Gardner: I told yall about Ike’s aunt in Keytesville.  She is the only person Ike has ever feared.  While intellectually bright, he is obstinate and stubborn.  He will go to his final grave, hating the Chiefs.  But, he hates everything.  He will finagle the finest thing into something bad. So no use in trying to convert him into a loyalist.  He doesn’t forget and forever, remembers how many times the Chiefs’ coach has made a fantastic fool of himself.  One more reason to vote against the Chiefs. Denver by 7 Lloyd “A Gentlemen’s Gentleman” Greenfield: Lloyd filters out the facts, when thinking about his prediction.  Never quickly, he fills his mind with facts and filters out the crap. He knows that 5-3 is respectable for the Chiefs and we should never forget that. He believes the Chiefs are a work in progress and he advises all of us to file that away.  He says it will be fun, not fouls on Sunday. Chiefs by 6 Ollie “Elephant Memory” Hubbard: Everybody is amazed how Ollie remembers everything. He focuses in on everything so that he can repeat it later, sometimes at the worst times.  He flags his memory with everything for he is an ace reporter.  It is fair to say that Ollie is aware of the Denver-Chiefs feud, going back to the good old days. But without Shanahan, the Broncos are in their final stages, at 2-6.  That’s fair enough for Ollie. Chiefs by 10 Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: He faces everything squarely and will not forfeit his right to speak.  Like Ollie, that Cleaver and Ike accuse him of fonduing the truth. That makes him furious and lose control.  One of the most loyal people around, he thinks it is futile to entertain any more flak from haters. Anyway you look at it, the Chiefs are gonna make the playoffs.  So, stop the fussing and cussing....a sure thing for Sunday. Chiefs by 10 Ed “Clearheaded And Competent”  West: Ed is a little shell-shot. In fact, he fears the lack of fundamentals that pervade the Chiefs, at times.  He blames the recent loss to Oakland because McCluster wasn’t there.  But fast and furious, Dexter will return and fly up and down the field on Sunday...bring Ed to fulfill his desire to see the Chiefs elevate. Chiefs by 7 Eric “Amanda And Erica’s Dad” Wesson:  Frankly, I thought that the officiating in the Raiders win was a little fickled, especially the fumble call that led to the Chiefs’ final score. Bowe finally caught a pass and finished with a touchdown. But, I am glad that the Raiders won as I predicted with a field goal in the final drive and final second of the game in overtime. I think that he has caught at least one pass for a touchdown in the last four games. As far as the Broncos I think the Chiefs will finally get out of their funk and squeak by the Broncos by a final score of 13 to 14.  Chiefs by 1. Final note:  The Chiefs are learning to play the game.  Winning means taking the bumps and bruises, as well as the roses and cheers.  And just think, we wrote this long article and never mentioned the most famous “F” word.  No need to use filth.  After all, it is all about the Chiefs. And we must stop talking about their funeral.  Ain’t gonna happen.

frames.text: Y’all remember Roberta Flack. She was quite the talk, back in the ‘60s and ‘70s. Her hit song, “Killing Me Softly”, found its way into all of our hearts and homes. But she sang another song, which is so appropriate for our “sinking fast” Chiefs. That song will be revealed after we talk a little about the New Orleans Saints, the Chiefs’ next opponent on Sunday. First of all, the Saints came into being as an NFL expansion team, back in the late ‘60s. Their rise to Super Bowl status has been phenomenal, especially since they had a rough, rough start. Some insensitive sportswriters once called them the “Aints”, owing to their winlessness. Now years later, we all have forgotten about those lean days and nowadays, always look to the Saints to be a contender to win the NFC South Division. Routinely now, they always play well against Division opponents like Atlanta, Carolina and Tampa Bay. But as of today, the Saints have not won a game, so far, this season. Some say it is the atmosphere. Recently, the Saints found themselves deep in controversy after the well-publicized bounty scheme. That fiasco left them without their head coach, Sean Payton, for all of this season. That penalty may well explain why the Saints are off to a rough start. But, what about the Chiefs? What can they say to explain another “shaky” beginning? What can the Chiefs do to make it all better? Actually, we, Monday Niters, believe the Saints will recover soon and start making championship plans. But not so for the Chiefs. Why is that so, you may ask. Well, this is where we talk again about Roberta Flack. Her “other” hit song was “The Closer I Get To You”. In that song, she is happy with the progress of her rising relationship. In fact, she proudly comments that her lover makes her “see” things more clearly. Well, the “closer”  we get to the Chiefs, the more we “see” how inept, how inadequate these bunch of bums are. Starting with the coaches, the front office and their regrettable quarterback, Matt Cassel. You don’t have to “get close” to see that these Chiefs are never gonna rise up. They are never gonna win our division again. They can stay here another 50 years and it will all be same. Full of excuses. Full of  explanations. And full of crap. And crap it is, no matter how close you get. In fact, we should start referring to them as the “Aints”. Because they aint gonna never be nothing.  So for Sunday’s game, it will be the Saints vs. the new Aints. And you don’t have to be “close” to predict the outcome. Roberta Flack would sang another song about the Chiefs. The farther I get from you, the better I seem to be. Monday Niters, what say you? Dr. Charles Allen           No big deal on being 0-2      Chiefs by 3 Paul Booker                   Winning in the “Big Easy”     Saints by 14 will not be easy Carl Clark                     Chiefs totally dysfunctional Saints by 10 Bubba Cleaver              Hope on!                                     Chiefs by 14 Ike Gardner                   Pioli, Cassel gotta go             Saints by 28 Lloyd Greenfield           This one is for Logan              Chiefs by 1 Ollie Hubbard                Saints go marching in              Saints by 40 Jim Nunnelly                 K.C. meets Hurricane Katrina Saints by 25 Ed West                        Saints will march all over K.C. Saints by 10

frames.text: Stewart Watson was a big, giant of a guy, who always wore a smile and had a baritone-like laugh. He was “at home” whereever he went, whether in his favorite club on Prospect or whether meeting you for the first time. He clearly will be missed by all of us Monday Niters for he was one of the founding members of this adult “boys club”.  To most of us, he had  been friends for all of his 24,582 days on this earth. But on July 3, of this year, “Bunny Rabbit” left this earth and thus, the basic reason for this column.   In short, we want to say “good bye” in a way that only friends who have known you a lifetime, can say it. So let’s start with “Bunny Rabbit” and his relentless use of nicknames. “Bunny Rabbit” had a nickname for everyone in our group. That’s because he wanted each of us to know that he liked each of us individually and collectively. Ollie was “Mr. Puddy Pot”  and Ike was “Huff”. Booker was “Chocolate Drop”. Dr. Allen was “Pumpkin” and Carl was appropriately called “Mr. Mary Lynn”. And because of my bald head, he started calling me “Mr. Peanut”. I dare say he would have to stop and think of our real names because that was all he called us, every day of his nearly 69 years.  We say nearly because he died just three days before his 69th birthday. And there was no denying him access to you. Even though he moved to St. Louis some years ago, he still managed to see everyone at least once a month or just calling them. Speaking of calling, “Bunny Rabbit” was a phone junkie.  Night or day, winter or fall, he would call one of us, out of the clear blue sky. It was as if we were his connection to reality or maybe he just wanted to stay close to his friends. Always the same, joy-induced greeting, “ what u doing boy?”. And then, right from there, the word would spread... “Bunny Rabbit” is in town and somehow, unplanned though it may be, there would be a reunion, right then and there. And it seemed he would always time his visit during one of our Monday Nite Footballers meeting and whatever the conversation on the floor, would give way to his one-man, nickname-calling comedy act.  “Bunny Rabbit” was a real friend and the kind of brother to everyone, even though he had no biological brothers or sisters. He exuded brotherhood, at its highest level.  In addition, “Bunny Rabbit” was a  lesson in kindness and consideration. He reminded us that we all must live our lives, merrily and among friends.  He demonstrated that by always dropping by and diverting you from your daily worries and strife. Yes, Bunny Rabbit was a spark of life to all of us and his light still shines in our thoughts and in our conversation. Ike says “Bunny Rabbit” always checked on him whether sick or well. And Ollie says that he has great memories of “Bunny” all the way from elementary school through Lincoln university.  But, Dr. Charles Allen concluded the stories about “Bunny Rabbit” best. He simply said that “Bunny Rabbit” extended a hand but he always touched our hearts. What else needs to be said but “Good Bye, ‘Bunny Rabbit’. We are all better off by knowing you and we will wear our nicknames proudly, in your honor.”

frames.text: John Legend wrote and dedicated a song to his recent bride. In that song, he just pours out his heart, telling her that “all of me loves all of you….your edges, your curves, and your perfect imperfections”. John Legend is saying that he realizes her love has some shortcomings, but he loves her deeply just the same. Now that’s just what most of us feel about our Chiefs. They have a perfect record but most of us are willing to live with their “perfect imperfections”. Some people even say the Chiefs are a fluke and are just waiting for them to show how imperfect they really are. But Paul Booker isn’t one of them. He’s been voting for the Chiefs all year long, despite voting against them all last year.  But Paul is more supportive this year. Always a Chiefs’ supporter ever since he came to town, way back in 1966. A veteran of the Air Force and a graduate of Lincoln university, Paul is a very likeable educator, having taught at Woodland, Switzer, Southeast Middle, Greenwood and C.A. Franklin schools. And he is generally healthy and is recovering graciously from the loss of his wife a few months ago. So these days, he is just trying to “maintain” and keep going. So the Chiefs are giving him the “perfect boost” that he needs.  Paul knows the Chiefs lack a consistent offense, even though the defensive unit is actually carrying the team. In spite of that, Paul expects the Chiefs to beat Denver on Sunday night. Yes, along with Ed West, Greenfield, Dr. Allen, Mrs. Banks and Ollie, Paul  is predicting a long-shot victory over the Manning-led Broncos. But his former boss, Ike Gardner and his 6902 buddy, Carl Clark, believes the Chiefs will succumb and lose, out in the mile-high city Paul and the other Chiefs supporters are thinking 10-0 and a sure-shot for the playoffs and maybe even the Western Division championship. But, not so fast. Ike and Carl are quick to point out the Chiefs’ imperfections. They say Manning will get rushed, even sacked a couple of times..but he will burn the “imperfect” secondary all night.  Conversely, both Booker and Cleaver remember the 100 yard interception return by Sean Smith and say proudly that the “perfect defense” will more than make up for any flaws in the Chiefs’ secondary. In fact, they say that “special D” has held all opponents to less than seventeen points, throughout all nine games.  All in all, all of us love all of the Chiefs. And we know it will be something to behold, if the Chiefs win it all. And if they don’t, we will still support them, in spite of their “imperfectness”. The Denver Broncos will be playing hard because they didn’t expect such an upsurge from the Chiefs. So, all eyes will be on the Chiefs, this Sunday night. National television. Suspect commentators. Possible championships. And like John Legend, we hope that those edges and imperfections don’t show up. At least, not Sunday night: Dr. Charles Allen: says “why change? The Chiefs are winning” Chiefs by 10 Mrs. Mila Banks:   It’s going to be a tight game, without a doubt. Chiefs by 3 Paul Booker:    Chiefs will crank up the “imperfect” offense. Chiefs by 7 Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: John Legend and Lisa Washington know about perfection. Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: John Legend and Lisa Washington know about perfection.                              Chiefs by 1

frames.text: This past Monday night, we talked a whole lot. A lot went down this week. Especially with the Chiefs’ victory and  the murder-suicide tragedy piercing the nation’s headlines. But, before we get to that, we had some community-minded guests to join us. One was Tony G from Hot 103 and the others were the Go-Along Club and Andre Jackmon, a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department at Swope Health Services. Thus, we want to tell you a little about them and then comment on Romeo’s leadership, through a double-crisis week with his team. • TONY G. . . for 19years, this young man has led the Toy and Food Drive for all of Kansas City. For this effort, he has been awarded boundless recognition but he still presents as eager as if it’s the very first time.  Many don’t know but Tony G  was a credible basketball player in the old Catholic leagues. Moreover, his name carried forwarded to the radio airways and he is featured each morning in “drive time”, delivering a morning start for thousands of metropolitan residents. He has also assisted in the development of the popular teen talk show, Generation Rap on Hot 103. But for Tony, this annual food event is just being a good neighbor. Having grown up near 39th and Prospect, Tony G just gives back to his community. In fact, he demonstrates his commitment year after year, making sure that families have food and kids have toys for Christmas. Big kudos for Tony G. • THE GO ALONG CLUB. . . This is group of middle-aged men who get together frequently. However, social-minded the group may appear, they raise thousands of dollars each year for college scholarships. They too were on-hand to talk about their community service, especially providing worthy students with money to go to college....raised through their own corporate resources. We cannot say enough about the men who help our community...each and every day. • ANDRE JACKSON, SWOPE HEALTH SERVICES. . . starting out as just a worker, Andre is now a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department. Andre is involved in establishing counseling and case management services, in and around schools. So far, he has mobilized many agencies and most important, helped his agency get services to those who need it. Andre is one of the rising young men in our community who defy the inappropriate stereotype of young black men. Andre called on us Monday Niters and the others to assist our children, even if just saying an encouraging word. He reiterated that our young people want and need our help. Well, what a night for Monday Niters. . . to hear and see our men, stepping up to help out in their community. Also, there was a lot of conversation about the Chiefs. Mainly, about Romeo and how he handled a team, wrought with confusion caused by the suicide of one  of the their fellow players. One that also included a murder of the player’s girlfriend. And one that required getting that team ready to play a game, the next day. So, we took a poll among our members and guests and commented on Romeo Crennel’s finest moment in his profession. On Sunday, Romeo will take his team back to his former place of employment, Cleveland. Where he once coached the Browns and now will return a national hero. Here’s what we think: Dr. Charles Allen:     Romeo was quite admirable this week.                   Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: He was outstanding handling all that pressure.   Browns by 10 Carl Clark: He did a good job but he didn’t save his.                 Browns by 10 Ike Gardner: He held it together. Because of that, I will pay  his bus fare to his next job. Browns by 3  Lloyd Greenfield:     He handled the situation, using family values.        Browns by 3 Jim Nunnelly: God must love Romeo. Chiefs by 7 Ed West: His demeanor saved the Chiefs....and his job.        Chiefs by 3 Joe Webster: Romeo earned himself one more year.                  Chiefs by 3 Andre Jackmon:     Romeo handled the media well...go Raiders         no prediction Hadley Reimal:     Admirable job under difficult circumstances.            Chiefs by 3 Ron Walton:           Return to Cleveland will return him to reality.             Browns by 10 Sanders Martin: Romeo should be back next year.                                Browns by 7 Willie Humphrey: Romeo did a helluva job getting the team up.           Browns by 7 Tom Brown: Romeo fate is still shaky, despite a good week. Browns by 7

frames.text: Editor, THE CALL: Each week during football season, I look forward to reading the “Monday Niters” predictions and the commentary by Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly. Mr. Nunnelly’s commentary in a recent “CALL” issue was particularly interesting as he told a little about each man in the “Monday Nite Footballers group.” Nunnelly is an excellent writer. He knows how to make words on a page come alive. Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men. In a recent  write-up, Nunnelly described these grandfathers of the group from Allen to West as: extraordinary, fantastic, effective, proud, steadfast, remarkable, complete, and encouraging. For what more could one ask? Monday Niters, “Keep on keeping on.” BRAVO!!.  Terry Strother Burlington, Iowa

frames.text: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Denver Broncos 12:00 p.m., KCTV  5 &hTab; &hTab; &hTab;&hTab;        Predictions (Wins In Parenthesis) Chatter, Conversation And Commentary &hTab;Well, Monday night, the Chiefs against Tennessee did not fold. And that's a good thing.  Those of us who are disillusioned optimists, might say*.the Chiefs are undefeated in December. &hTab;This statement begs the question*.. "what does that mean".  Absolutely, nothing.  But, it does say loudly that some bad coaching occurred, somewhere.  For how can a running back be near-released one week and run two 40-yards-plus touchdowns on another.  Where has Johnson been and why hasn't he been playing?  Who held him back? &hTab; Was it all because he responded to a coach's inappropriate comments?  We really do know what the deal is, don't we? Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men. frames.text: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Minnesota Vikings 4:00 p.m., WDAF-TV&punctSpace;4 &hTab; &hTab; &hTab;&hTab;        Predictions (Wins In Parenthesis) Chatter, Conversation And Commentary It is different, with the Chiefs, these days. Already won the AFC West Division. So, what’s next.  Well, Sunday, the Chiefs  will move on to Minnesota and puruse  homefield guarantee.  While the Chiefs struggle to keep opposing running backs from openly devouring us, the Chiefs are sporting a large-scale, league-leading offense.  One that features an All-Pro running back, a late-rising quarterback, and a herd of unstoppable receivers.  And while everybody knows the almost-unblemished offense, every one still thinks the run defense will eventually run us down.  But, weak defense or not, tomorrow’s game rest solely on how well the Chiefs are able to contain the Culpepper-Moss connection. Either way, look for Warfield, Wesley, and Woods to have their hands full.  Moreover, the same defensive line that allowed Clinton Portis, through the cracks, will now have to rush and deck Culpepper.  Just like covering Moss, sacking Culpepper will be a formidable task.  Ike thinks Minnesota will win.  He’s back, y’all.  All he needed was a resounding Chiefs’ loss, and here he comes with that Chiefs-bashing stuff, again.  Don’t worry, the Chiefs will be watching Sunday, to see if they are closer to homefield advantage, throughout the playoffs.  Happy Holidays!

frames.text: Now, let’s get real.  The Chiefs are wishing that Sunday’s game was still pre-season.  That way, they could evaluate the new players, rest the old ones at the end of the first quarter, and then dodge the brutal, candid questions, asked by  blood-sucking reporters after the game. But, it is “for real” now.  Sunday will open the biggest wound possible in Herm Edwards’ armor.  It will show that the Chiefs are destined for another dismal season. In addition, Sunday will show that the draft, trades, and  the legacy were all worthless and unfulfilling.  The Chiefs  have too many unknown and untried players, to even think about beating the Patriots.  In fact, we should fast forward this game and go directly to the next two games..against Oakland at home and Atlanta away.  The Chiefs just might beat Oakland, depending on how well Russell, their strong-armed quarterback, plays.  And maybe just maybe we might beat the Vick-less Falcons.  If my math is right, three weeks from now we will be 2-1. But, come Sunday, they will lose so badly that we will think there is another Boston Massacre.  Even those little men on the New England helmets will dance in both end zones.  Tom Brady will pick  our hand-made secondary apart.  And except for a couple of long runs, the Chiefs will appear like they are still in pre-season mode.  Once again, Herm will pick up where he left off, last season.  With an inadequately profound statement that says and does nothing.  And the reporters will laughingly write the same stories that they wrote all  of last year, about how unlikely the Chiefs are to win at all. And the fans will and should direct our attention to  Oakland and Atlanta, the Chiefs’ next two opponents. And Herm will go to work on his next appearance before the reporters, hopefully more realistic.  For now, though. . . look for the Patriots to beat the Chiefs by at least 30 points.  Enough said. Now, let’s get real. The Chiefs are wishing that Sunday’s game was still pre-season. That way, they could evaluate the new players, rest the old ones at the end of the first quarter, and then dodge the brutal, candid questions, asked by blood-sucking reporters after the game.

But, it is “for real” now. Sunday will open the biggest wound possible in Herm Edwards’ armor. It will show that the Chiefs are destined for another dismal season.

In addition, Sunday will show that the draft, trades, and the legacy were all worthless and unfulfilling.

The Chiefs have too many unknown and untried players, to even think about beating the Patriots. In fact, we should fast forward this game and go directly to the next two games..against Oakland at home and Atlanta away. The Chiefs just might beat Oakland, depending on how well Russell, their strong-armed quarterback, plays. And maybe just maybe we might beat the Vick-less Falcons. If my math is right, three weeks from now we will be 2-1. But, come Sunday, they will lose so badly that we will think there is another Boston Massacre. Even those little men on the New England helmets will dance in both end zones. Tom Brady will pick our hand-made secondary apart. And except for a couple of long runs, the Chiefs will appear like they are still in pre-season mode. Once again, Herm will pick up where he left off, last season. With an inadequately profound statement that says and does nothing. And the reporters will laughingly write the same stories that they wrote all of last year, about how unlikely the Chiefs are to win at all. And the fans will and should direct our attention to Oakland and Atlanta, the Chiefs’ next two opponents. And Herm will go to work on his next appearance before the reporters, hopefully more realistic. For now, though. . . look for the Patriots to beat the Chiefs by at least 30 points.

Enough said.

frames.text: It’s Friday and we are still gloating over the Chiefs victory over Denver, last Sunday.  It seems like it was a dream and soon we will all wake up to reality. . . that the Chiefs will return to their losing ways, this Sunday against Carolina.  Most of the guys felt like Carolina will topple the Chiefs and Herm Edwards will return to his confusing testimony about the plight of the 2008 Chiefs.   By the way, did you notice how ol” Herm hugged Larry Johnson after the last Kansas City touchdown.  He whispered in Larry’s ear “thanks for saving my job, man”.  And then later, Carl Peterson came out of his suite and said essentially the same...”you gave me one more year, LJ..I apologize for putting you on the bench”.   No doubt about it LJ saved the day for these two.  Already the St. Louis Rams have fired their coach.  And guess who is next if we don’t play well against Carolina?  But last Monday night, we spent most of our time talking about the how our old-time teachers influenced us.  Thus, we remembered them. DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Thinks the Kansas City School District suffers from negative press. . . thanks his former teacher, Luke Ponder for clearing the path for him to attend college on an acting scholarship. . . acting or not, Charles thinks the Chiefs are in a winning mode..Chiefs by 7 PAUL BOOKER:  Sometimes called the Apostle Paul. . .Thinks that more parental involvement is needed. . . believes the Carolina moon will not shine on the Chiefs...Carolina by 13. CARL CLARK:  Is a proponent of teachers taking tests for certification. . . is a stickler for accountability. . . in or out of trouble, begs the Chiefs not to get too happy because they are still losers. . . Carolina by 14 IKE GARDNER:  Grandson Isaiah often sings at St. James...says that when kids are going to private schools, they are saying that education is a valued asset. . . likes Christmas but believes Santa only comes once a year for the Chiefs...Carolina by 17 LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Feels the teaching curriculum needs to be upgraded...and teachers ought to go back to basics in education. . . .thinks the Chiefs can lose all the games...Carolina by 7. JIM NUNNELLY:  Favorite teacher was the school secretary, Beulah Ralph, who taught him about school administration...took time with him...believes principals needs executive coaching to achieve goals. . . .corporate or not, the Chiefs will win their second game in a row because the defense will give Larry Johnson more opportunities. . .Chiefs by 10 ED WEST:  Feels the Chiefs will start another losing streak against Carolina. . . feels that teachers pre-judge most black kids without really knowing their assets. . . Chiefs won’t overcome losing label. . . Carolina by 14.  OLLIE HUBBARD:  Need to increase the amount of homework, especially in math and reading. . . homework is instruction hours and they help out in test scores. . . parents must help. . . last week, the Chiefs made it sooooo goooooood, let’s keep it up. . . Chiefs by 14 BUBBA CLEAVER:  In Washington this, dealing with the bailout. . . voted against first package because it did not contain enough provisions to help everyday people.. . . is actively campaigning on behalf of Obama. . . thinks the Chiefs’ win over Denver was a fluke. . . thus, Carolina by 10.

frames.text: George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs

frames.text: Do you remember “The Jeffersons”?  That was a tv show that appeared regularly on CBS, way back in the seventies. This was a Norman Lear production, that attempted to show that black people were “moving on up”. In fact, the show took place in the Jeffersons’ Fifth Avenue apartment, on the upper East Side of New York City. And since the prosperity was all new to the Jeffersons, the writers traced their humorous, everyday activities. Some of it was funny but the whole thing was filled with a lot of fantasy. Speaking of fantasy, the Chiefs have been living on “Fantasy Island”. For the first nine games the Chiefs were the ‘talk of the sports world”. They were undefeated until they met the Payton-laced Denver Broncos. Then the Chargers. Then, the Broncos again. And just like that, the little “fantasy” bubble began to bust. In fact, these same Chiefs lost five of their next seven games, the latest being to the Chargers last Sunday. Talk about up and down. The Chiefs were living in a fantasy world and it all came tumbling down, causing many to mentally eliminate the Chiefs from further contention. But is it over for the Chiefs? Now remember the Chiefs were 2-14 in 2013. And now they are in playoffs and have been there solidly for three weeks running. They didn’t need help from other teams, they clinched a spot and just waited. So, my point is that the “fantasy” continues, in spite of them losing the last third of the season. And last Sunday, they lost but they didn’t use twenty of the first twenty two starters. So, San Diego beat the second and third teamers of the Chiefs. Not Jamaal Charles or Tamba Hali or Derrick Johnson or Dwayne Bowe. So what’s the point? The most salient point is that the Chiefs are still pursuing the NFL Super Bowl game.. Even Carl Clark says let’s support the Chiefs “for the heck of it”. As always, that Paul Booker and Ike Gardner are non-supportive, believing that the Chiefs will lose their first round playoff game to Indianapolis Colts, just like they did a couple of weeks ago.And for sure, that will be “it” for Kansas City and its fantasy season. Hold up for a minute!. The Chiefs did put eight players on the All-Pro roster. And their coach, Andy Reid, will probably be Coach Of The Year. And some second teamers are going to playing a lot, come Sunday afternoon. Thereby, making the Chiefs even better prepared for the upcoming game. Bottom line, like the Jeffersons. . . the Chiefs are “moving on up”. They finally got a piece of the NFL pie. Now Ike will probably predict against the Chiefs. But you all know Ike. He was wrong eleven of sixteen times this year. That means he wasn’t right, most of the time, about the Chiefs. He is not the “Holy Grail” of predicting football games. So, let’s get behind our hometown team and maybe, just maybe….we can “move further on up” to the East side and take on New England and then onto the West side to take on Denver. Wait. Wait. Wait. I’ve drifted back into Fantasy Land. For right now, Chiefs over the Colts. (We hope).

George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs

Do you remember “The Jeffersons”?

That was a tv show that appeared regularly on CBS, way back in the seventies. This was a Norman Lear production, that attempted to show that black people were “moving on up”. In fact, the show took place in the Jeffersons’ Fifth Avenue apartment, on the upper East Side of New York City. And since the prosperity was all new to the Jeffersons, the writers traced their humorous, everyday activities. Some of it was funny but the whole thing was filled with a lot of fantasy.

Speaking of fantasy, the Chiefs have been living on “Fantasy Island”. For the first nine games the Chiefs were the ‘talk of the sports world”. They were undefeated until they met the Payton-laced Denver Broncos. Then the Chargers. Then, the Broncos again. And just like that, the little “fantasy” bubble began to bust. In fact, these same Chiefs lost five of their next seven games, the latest being to the Chargers last Sunday. Talk about up and down. The Chiefs were living in a fantasy world and it all came tumbling down, causing many to mentally eliminate the Chiefs from further contention.

But is it over for the Chiefs? Now remember the Chiefs were 2-14 in 2013. And now they are in playoffs and have been there solidly for three weeks running. They didn’t need help from other teams, they clinched a spot and just waited. So, my point is that the “fantasy” continues, in spite of them losing the last third of the season. And last Sunday, they lost but they didn’t use twenty of the first twenty two starters. So, San Diego beat the second and third teamers of the Chiefs. Not Jamaal Charles or Tamba Hali or Derrick Johnson or Dwayne Bowe.

So what’s the point? The most salient point is that the Chiefs are still pursuing the NFL Super Bowl game.. Even Carl Clark says let’s support the Chiefs “for the heck of it”. As always, that Paul Booker and Ike Gardner are non-supportive, believing that the Chiefs will lose their first round playoff game to Indianapolis Colts, just like they did a couple of weeks ago.And for sure, that will be “it” for Kansas City and its fantasy season.

Hold up for a minute!. The Chiefs did put eight players on the All-Pro roster. And their coach, Andy Reid, will probably be Coach Of The Year. And some second teamers are going to playing a lot, come Sunday afternoon. Thereby, making the Chiefs even better prepared for the upcoming game.

Bottom line, like the Jeffersons. . . the Chiefs are “moving on up”. They finally got a piece of the NFL pie. Now Ike will probably predict against the Chiefs. But you all know Ike. He was wrong eleven of sixteen times this year. That means he wasn’t right, most of the time, about the Chiefs. He is not the “Holy Grail” of predicting football games.

So, let’s get behind our hometown team and maybe, just maybe….we can “move further on up” to the East side and take on New England and then onto the West side to take on Denver. Wait. Wait. Wait. I’ve drifted back into Fantasy Land.

For right now, Chiefs over the Colts. (We hope).

Scholarship Information Night

frames.text: &hTab;Donnelly Colege will offer a Scholarship Information Night on Monday, Feb. 16, from 6:30-8:30 p.m., in the first floor Meeting Room.  Participants need to make a reservation by calling (913) 621-8700. &hTab;At the session, students will learn how to get free money to attend Donnelly College.  Presenters will explain how to apply for Presidential and Bloch Scholarships which cover tuition, fees and books.  They will also learn about federal Pell Grants and Kansas comprehensive Grants for low-income students.  All students with a GPA of 2.5 or above, who participate in the Scholarship Night, will be awarded a minimum scholarship of $500 to be used at Donnelly College for tuition not covered by grants. &hTab;“Limited financial resources are no obstacle for attending college,” said Sister Mary Agnes Patterson, Donnelly Vice-President.  “There are grants and scholarships available for those who qualify.  And starting at a local college like Donnelly saves students the cost of living in a dorm and allows them to work part-time.”&hTab;

frames.text: MONDAY&punctSpace;NITERS&punctSpace;VISIT&punctSpace;WITH&punctSpace;FORMER&punctSpace;CHIEFS&punctSpace;GREAT. . . Otis Taylor, former Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver, was the guest of honor recently at the Monday Nite Footballers meeting, at Rev. Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver’s house. He shared excerpts from his autobiography, “Otis Taylor” by Otis Taylor. The book recounts Otis’ days here, in the 60s and 70s. Len Dawson, Hall of Fame quarterback, wrote the foreword and called Otis “a big play receiver”. More important, Otis listened to Monday Niters as they remembered his spectacular one-hand catches and subsequent long runs. Carl Clark was able to see a picture of his most memorable Chiefs’ plays, when Taylor carried Pat Fischer across the goal line on his back. Many, including Ollie Gates and Rev. Cleaver,  have tried to get Otis inducted into the NFL&punctSpace;Hall of Fame, but to no avail. Otis played college football at&punctSpace;Prairie View A&M during the same time Rev. Cleaver was there. Because of an advanced illness, Otis has been walking with the assistance of a cane. He was a frequent customer at Maxine’s, 31st and Benton.

frames.text: Brandon Lloyd, Alicia Keys, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Brandon Lloyd, Alicia Keys, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Did you hear about the butt-kicking New England handed the league-leading Houston Texans, last Monday night. We gathered over to Ed West’s, to watch what we thought would be a good game. It didn’t happen. The Brady Bunch slaughtered the Texans, 42-14, with Brady tossing four touchdown passes.  On the bright spot is that game was Kansas City’s own, Brandon Lloyd. We remember Brandon’s high school days out at Blue Springs. From there, he went on to star at wide receiver, at the University of Illinois. And then, he has caught passes for the Denver Broncos, the St. Louis Rams and now the New England Patriots. Known for his acrobatic catches, this guy is “on fire”. It is not every receiver who has the best passer in NFL history as his passing mate. Look for more. Speaking of being “on fire”. Have you heard Alicia Keys’ latest CD, “This Girl Is On Fire”. It is selling like wildfire. If you have seen the video, she paints the story of a young woman, taking on the struggles and joys of life. Not to be outdone, she has to be “on fire”, just to make it. This song has rapidly become the spokes-song for millions of young women, adrift in this world. But, to me, her CD begs the question. . . who is NOT “on fire”. You guessed it. It’s the Kansas City Chiefs. Two buckets of gasoline and a box of matches won’t light up the Chiefs, these days.  They have been down so long that “getting up” don’t even cross their minds. With only two wins again eleven losses, the network commentators don’t even comment on the score, demonstrating their neglect of and disdain for these Chiefs. In fact, talking about the Chiefs was so dull. . . that we found ourselves talking about Robert Griffin III. . . the old time Georgy Burger. . . how integration killed the economic spirit of 18th and 12th streets. . . Tom Brady’s record of a passing touchdown for forty two consecutive games. . . Charles Kynard, premier organist who played at the Blue Room in the sixties...how the post office, the school district and the automotive industry were the plum jobs of the ‘50s, ‘60s, and ‘70s. . . how Carl Clark ignored the state-line boundaries and found Mary Lynn in Kansas City, Kas. Actually, our discussion had more “fire” than the Chiefs have. In fact, our discussion soon landed into a healthy respect of years-gone-by.  When we were all in one neighborhood and acted and thought unity. When our business owners were our neighbors and our churches were our uniform resource. Yes, when the Chiefs could walk on water, while being “on fire” at the same time. When being from Kansas City was something to behold. . . not to silently mention, in passing. Where did it all go? We don’t know but we wish we had those same pride-filled moments back. And it won’t get any better out in Oakland, this coming Sunday.  The Monday Niters have given up on the Chiefs and all that they stand/stood for. Bottom line, the “fire next time” is a long time away. Charles Allen: I’m holding on. Chiefs by 3 Paul Booker:  No joy in Muddville.  Raiders by 10 Carl Clark: Chiefs are done!       Raiders by 10 Ike Gardner: Chiefs will lose in the Black Hole. Raiders by 13 Lloyd Greenfield: Chiefs are a broken vessel. Raiders by 14  Ollie Hubbard:  I’m praying at Ebenezer.  Toss-up Jim Nunnelly: Fire is out for Romeo. Raiders by 7 Ed West: No Bowe, no go!                Raiders by 10

On the bright spot is that game was Kansas City’s own, Brandon Lloyd. We remember Brandon’s high school days out at Blue Springs. From there, he went on to star at wide receiver, at the University of Illinois. And then, he has caught passes for the Denver Broncos, the St. Louis Rams and now the New England Patriots. Known for his acrobatic catches, this guy is “on fire”. It is not every receiver who has the best passer in NFL history as his passing mate. Look for more.

Speaking of being “on fire”. Have you heard Alicia Keys’ latest CD, “This Girl Is On Fire”. It is selling like wildfire. If you have seen the video, she paints the story of a young woman, taking on the struggles and joys of life. Not to be outdone, she has to be “on fire”, just to make it. This song has rapidly become the spokes-song for millions of young women, adrift in this world. But, to me, her CD begs the question. . . who is NOT “on fire”. You guessed it. It’s the Kansas City Chiefs. Two buckets of gasoline and a box of matches won’t light up the Chiefs, these days.

They have been down so long that “getting up” don’t even cross their minds. With only two wins again eleven losses, the network commentators don’t even comment on the score, demonstrating their neglect of and disdain for these Chiefs. frames.text: Shakespeare, Some Common Quotes, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Shakespeare, Some Common Quotes, And The Chiefs

frames.text: When the Chiefs are losing, we search hard for something to talk about. And since the Chiefs have won just one game, we found ourselves talking about something odd. . . William Shakespeare, the best known playwright in the English language.  Now, this genius wrote thirty eight plays and many poems, as far back as five hundred years ago. Besides the Bible, his works are quoted more than any other form of literature. His most notable plays include Macbeth, Othello, Richard III, and Midsummer Night’s Dream. And Shakespeare was quite versatile. . . having wrote comedies, histories, character studies and a lot about politics.  What would Shakespeare have said about the Chiefs? We will find out, after looking closer at Sunday’s game against the barely-alive Oakland Raiders. First, a little about Oakland. Like the Chiefs, the Raiders were part of the old American Football League, starting way back in 1960. Right away, the Chiefs and the Raiders became rivals, playing some real close games both at Municipal Stadium and the “Black Hole”. And somewhere along the line, the games would end up with a fight or two. Commonly called the “Silver and Black”, the Raiders have struggled in recent years. But they have won three Super Bowls, way back in 1976, 1980, and 1987.  Surprisingly, they also have 13 players in the illustrious Football Hall Of Fame, in Canton, Ohio. But all that won’t matter when they come marching into Arrowhead at noon on Sunday. The Chiefs’ fans will heckle the pirate-dressed Raiders’ fans and “there will be no peace”. The Chiefs will be trying to beat their division rival because they have only beaten San Diego this year. And Oakland will be trying to remain off the bottom, where the Chiefs currently reside. So while no championship will be at stake, it promises to be a first-rate battle. Shakespeare would have spoken a special quote for this meaningless game. “To be or not to be, that is the question.” In response, the Monday Niters actually applied many of the famous quotes from Shakespeare to their predictions. Some of them are quite creative, so please  applaud these old men for paying attention in school. Ike actually took a college class in Shakespeare. And Loyal Lloyd has acted in a Shakespeare play or two. And Congressman Cleaver has used Shakespeare as part of his many sermons. While the rest of us have unknowingly quoted Shakespeare hundreds of times. So sit back and enjoy finding out that Shakespeare is all around us, even on a Monday night, at a boring football meeting. Dr. Charles Allen, Luck has prevailed with the Raiders.           Chiefs by 14 Paul Booker, “Romeo, Romeo, where art thou?” Raiders by 10 Carl Clark, Thou has to win, sometimes. Chiefs by 3 Congressman Emanuel Cleaver, “If music be the food of love, play on”.      Chiefs by 10 Ike Gardner, “Full of sound and fury, signifying nothing”. Raiders by 10 Lloyd Greenfield, “Victoria’s blood, it warms thy heart”.         Chiefs by 3 Ollie Hubbard, “Expectations is the root of all heartaches” Chiefs by 3 Jim Nunnelly, “All is well that ends well”. Chiefs by 7 Ed West, “Not to be, that is the answer”.  Raiders by 10 Eric “Amanda, Bri, and Erica’s Dad” Wesson, “Hark another loss for the Chiefs”. Raiders by 3

frames.text: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Denver Broncos 3:15  p.m., KCTV 5 Carl Clark (7)            Denver by 14 Chiefs are going in the "right" direction (downward)! Bubba Cleaver (6)     Denver by 10 Broncos kicking the Chiefs for the second time! Ike Gardner (6)         Denver by 17 Chiefs have forfeited their credibility! Ed West (6)               Denver by 14 Chiefs waiting to exhale! Paul Booker (5)        It’ll be a MILE-HIGH event! Lloyd Greenfield(5) Denver by 3 Len Dawson for offensive coordinator! Jim Nunnelly (5)        KC by 3 Gonzalez, Parker, Smith and Allen say the buck stops here! Charles Allen (4)        KC by 3 Chiefs still have a shot at second place! The Chiefs, St. James, and Ten Dead Flies Ike, Carl, and Ed all attend St. James United Methodist Church. In fact, when it comes to activities, their church ranks second-to-none. Now what does that fact have to do with a bunch of old men, talking about football every Monday night. Unlike most other Monday nights, the conversation, chatter and commentary have slowly drifted away from the Chiefs. That’s because the locals keep losing and it is senseless to keep boarding a sinking ship. Thus, these chatters are scrambling to find something good to talk about. A frustrated minister, Ike out-of-the-clear-blue asked if New England would go undefeated in 2007? Unlike Carl, Ike and Ed quickly said that the Patriots would certainly go unbeaten. Every one else, including Greenfield, Booker and Dr. Allen, felt that New England would lose at least one game. Ideally, they all would be chatting about the Chiefs if it weren’t for this tag-team we call the Chiefs. But, like so many other fans, these Monday Niters have switched their conversational loyalties. . .this time to arguably the best team ever in the history of the National Football League. And this Sunday, the no-loss Patriots will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers, a perennial contender. It will be “the” game-to-watch. Brady will be Brady and somehow, just like against Baltimore, the Patriots will emerge at 13-0. For the record, all of these guys, except Dr. Allen and me, think that Broncos will annihilate the Chiefs on Sunday in Denver. And then Sunday evening just after “60 Minutes”, they will all go back to talking about St. James or something else that’s positive. That’s because the Chiefs ain’t worth ten dead flies. Go Patriots, go!

Chiefs are going in the "right" direction

Bubba Cleaver (6)     Denver by 10
Broncos kicking the Chiefs for the second
time!
Ike Gardner (6)         Denver by 17
Chiefs have forfeited their credibility!
Ed West (6)               Denver by 14
Chiefs waiting to exhale!
Paul Booker (5)        It’ll be a MILE-HIGH event!
Lloyd Greenfield(5) Denver by 3
Len Dawson for offensive coordinator!
Jim Nunnelly (5)        KC by 3
Gonzalez, Parker, Smith and Allen say the buck stops here!
Charles Allen (4)        KC by 3
Chiefs still have a shot at second place!
The Chiefs, St. James, and Ten Dead Flies
Ike, Carl, and Ed all attend St. James United Methodist Church. In fact, when it comes to activities, their church ranks second-to-none.
Now what does that fact have to do with a bunch of old men, talking about football every Monday night. Unlike most other Monday nights, the conversation, chatter and commentary have slowly drifted away from the Chiefs. That’s because the locals keep losing and it is senseless to keep boarding a sinking ship. Thus, these chatters are scrambling to find something good to talk about.
A frustrated minister, Ike out-of-the-clear-blue asked if New England would go undefeated in 2007? Unlike Carl, Ike and Ed quickly said that the Patriots would certainly go unbeaten. Every one else, including Greenfield, Booker and Dr. Allen, felt that New England would lose at least one game. Ideally, they all would be chatting about the Chiefs if it weren’t for this tag-team we call the Chiefs. But, like so many other fans, these Monday Niters have switched their conversational loyalties. . .this time to arguably the best team ever in the history of the National Football League. And this Sunday, the no-loss Patriots will take on the Pittsburgh Steelers, a perennial contender. It will be “the” game-to-watch. Brady will be Brady and somehow, just like against Baltimore, the Patriots will emerge at 13-0. For the record, all of these guys, except Dr. Allen and me, think that Broncos will annihilate the Chiefs on Sunday in Denver. And then Sunday evening just after “60 Minutes”, they will all go back to talking about St. James or something else that’s positive. That’s because the Chiefs ain’t worth ten dead flies. Go Patriots, go!

frames.text: Where have the legacy gone, the ones on brought on by Buck Buchanan, Willie Lanier, Emmitt Thomas and Otis Taylor?  The Chiefs suck and made us reminsce about the “good old days” when win or lose, fans felt good about our home-town Chiefs.   But after Sunday’s brutal beating by Oakland, we are convinced that the Chiefs could not even beat Raytown Middle School Blue Jays.  And the coaching was as bad as it has ever been.  From the grave, Hank Stram would ask Herm. . . “what the hell are you doing with my team”?  And pulling Larry Johnson from the line-up cashed in any hope we had of winning.   Just don’t know about these Chiefs.  If we put Larry back in the line-up and run him 30 times, we just might win Sunday.  Otherwise, Paul, Carl, Bubba, Ike, Ollie, Lloyd and Ed are right.  Just Charles and I think the legacy will return.  Hopefully! DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Graduated from UMKC Dental School at age 38. . . gets inward satisfaction from providing needed dental services. . . Catholic by faith. . . a man of a few words but delivers exactly what he promises. . . mentors young professionals. . . known to hang out every once in a while (every dat). . . has never predicted against the Chiefs. . . though he is thoroughly disappointed with but hopeful for the Chiefs. . . Chiefs by 3. PAUL BOOKER:  Will celebrate his 72nd birthday in November. . . has perfect attendance at the 6902 School. . . believes today’s teenagers are smarter than their parents, which makes the role for grandparents very important. . . has taken an annual physical each year for the past fifty years. . . doesn’t smoke but will take a sip or two or three or four. . . thinks the Chiefs are busted and will not beat the Falcons.. . . no way, no how. . . Atlanta by; 13 CARL CLARK: A Navy veteran...a vice president of the Ivanhoe Club, one of the oldest social clubs in our community. . . planning a trip to Martha’s vineyard. . . went to Indonesia and thought it was Paradise...loves to argue about everything...but no argument about this week’s prediction. . . believes the Chiefs have too many problems to win. . . Atlanta by 14. BUBBA CLEAVER:  Has three spoiled grandchildren. . . has real inside knowledge on foreclosures. . . played college football with Otis Taylor. . . lives three blocks from the United States Capitol. . . .number one goal is to get Obama elected. . . spends big and...shops furiously at the area’s best thrift stores. . . believes the Chiefs’ snowball is rolling downhill. . . Atlanta by 10. IKE GARDNER:  Joined the Alphas at Howard University way back in 1954. . . attended Lincoln High School, later taught psychology, math, and science there. . . feels strongly that black men should eat appropriately and exercise regularly. . . has a tendency to tell the same story over and over and over. . . but his story against the Chiefs never changes. . . He says the Chiefs have no offense, no defense, and no coach. . .well all right now, Atlanta by 30. LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Made sure that the Monday Nite Footballers joined as Life Members of the NAACP. . . s working on purchasing a table at the October 18 annual dinner.. . . spoils his grandchild but not too much. . . wife also a patron of the arts. . . balding beyond belief. . . speaks with authority about the Chiefs’ upcoming loss on Sunday.. . . Atlanta by 7. JIM NUNNELLY:   Goes by the moniker “Grand Dad”...retiring from Jackson County at the end of year. . . will consult with local organizations afterwards. . . provides the best recommendation letters for teenagers going off to college. . . still will not patronize Shell gas stations because of racial remarks made a 10 years ago. . .has a very quiet demeanor. believes Chiefs should resurrect Larry Johnson and thus, beat Atlanta. . . Chiefs by 3. ED WEST:  Insisted on sauna in his fantastic house...a body of a 40-year-old (now 70 plus). . . grew up in Osawatomie, Kas. . . one of first African American supervisors at old Western Electric. . . believes that Obama has a chance to win if  he can do something about this economy. . . won a national award for falling asleep the fastest...favorite song “wake me when it’s over”. . . believes the Chiefs cannot win because no offense, no defense, equals no win. . . Atlanta by 10.

frames.text: Okay. Okay.  The Chiefs are losing and do we need to keep talk about the “dead and buried”?   Many of our Monday Niters have written off the Chiefs for 2008.  Larry Johnson hasn’t helped with his off-the-field shenanigans.  And the lack of an NFL-status quarterback complicates an already dismal season.  And to make matters worse, every one is asking who will the first to get the ax. . . Carl Peterson or Herm Edwards.  To Elize and Clyde in Oakland, I am ready to concede our bet and just not talk about the Chiefs anymore.  So, we Monday Niters talked about the ensuing, history-making election. DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Charles says he will vote early, on his way into work. . .Charles says his office staff can take as long as it takes to vote. . . is Chiefs are struggling right now, having only a 1-4 record. . .Charles just won’t give up. . .Chiefs by 3 PAUL BOOKER:   Paul will be out of town on November 4. . . he is considering voting absentee on that day. . . Paul believes that the Chiefs are a dysfunctional family. . .Jets by 20. CARL CLARK:  Carl will vote in the mid-morning, avoiding the on-the-way-to-work rush. . .Carl will never vote again for those Chiefs. . . Jets by 20 BUBBA CLEAVER:   Praised his fellow Monday Niters for being so knowledgeable about election stuff. . .he has helped Obama campaign in Minnesota and Georgia and is being asked to go to Ohio and Arizona soon. . .It IS written that the Chiefs will lose badly in New York. . . Jets by 12 IKE GARDNER:  Ike first voted for Adlai Stevenson way back in 1956. . . he is guaranteeing that his adult children will vote for Obama. . . saying the Chiefs are gathering steam as the roll downhill...Jets by 35. LLOYD GREENFIELD : Lloyd votes at Grace Point Church at 104th and Blue River Road. . . he will vote electronically. . .thinks we ought to plan a memorial services for the departed Chiefs. . .Jets by 20 OLLIE HUBBARD:  Ollie is the only Monday Niter who has already voted. . . he voted absentee because of his leg disability. . .Ollie always votes for the team that the Chiefs are playing. . .this time, no exception. . . Jets by 40. JIM NUNNELLY:   He is concerned that people who think they have lost their right to vote. . . if you are awaiting trial in jail and have not been convicted, you can still vote absentee. . . Brett Favre can be beat....Chiefs by 3 (He too is letting the election of Obama get to him!) ED WEST:   Like Obama, has Kansas connections.. . .he was was born in rural Osawatomie. . . he voted for Kennedy for the first time way back in 1960. . . thinks the Chiefs are an NFL team anymore...no offense, no defense, no win. . . Jets by 30.

frames.text: Man, it was so hard to talk about the Kansas City Chiefs in serious manner.   In fact, Ed West recognized that the Chiefs played better. frames.text: Chatter, Conversation and Commentary Super Bowl 42,  No Competition February is Black History Month. It’s also the month when 22 states will decide its presidential preference. Of lesser importance, it is also the birthday month of our nation’s founding president, George Washington. And for lovers, the month houses Valentine’s Day. But all this will not hold a candle to Super Bowl 42, featuring the undefeated-going-perfect New England Patriots against the never-quitting New York Giants.  But, the game is only a small part. People will be talking about the million-dollar commercials. Already, one sponsor has set aside 16 million to be first in the commercial queue. Add to that the multi-million dollar half-time show (people are still talking about the Janet Jackson fiasco). And most of all, folks are lining the pockets of the Las Vegas casinos. . . rying to pick a for-sure winner. Right now, New England has the edge and everybody is talking about the Brady to Toomer nexus. But what about Little, less-famous brother Eli Manning.  Now, that is the real story of this Super Bowl. For nearly ten years, everybody has been talking about Big Brother, Priceless Peyton. And for  the record, he was supposed to lead the Colts into Phoenix. Instead, it was Eli who is going to the Big Ball. There is hope for us all. Which brings me to my real message about the Monday Nite Footballers Group. As we all elderize, we can go back to Super Bowl One and Four and any other. We saw Doug Williams set a Super Bowl record for most touchdowns scored in a Super Bowl. We’ve even witnessed running backs like Terrell Davis gallop from one end of the stadium to the other. We’ve known Kansas Citians, like Ralph Brown, who always went to the Super Bowl.  And finally, we remembered way back when the Chiefs were in the Super Bowl. I believe it was against Minnesota. I believe it was Otis Taylor who starred that day. He made a little kick going into the end zone.  Pardon us for not being sure about all the details. . . for it has been 39 years since the Chiefs were there. Hint. Hint. Do you hear us, Peterson and Edwards?

frames.text: Watch for the Tyler Thigpen shirts to start emerging.   After all, this boy is the “only” hopes for our pitiful Chiefs.  He not only is helping the Chiefs on the field but is helping Carl and Herm keep their jobs.   All of a sudden, the Chiefs went from a “last place” team to a “team in the process of re-building”.  And for the record, Larry Johnson better watch out.   We all have seen people who get so big in the head that they think the world can’t operated without them.  Well, even though the Chiefs are still losing, they don’t look as bad in their losing effort.  They have a little swagger.   Did you ever think you’d see Herm Edwards go for two points?  Thank God he is truly being converted.  Remember when all he talked about was “THE defense”.   And do you all remember last week when Thigpen scored a touchdown, as a receiver?   Pretty soon, ol’ Herm will start acting like a real head coach, not just an entitled defensive coordinator. Watch for the pundits to start counting the one and two point losses, as Chiefs’ win! Enough about the Chiefs.   At Paul Booker’s house, we talked about volunteering.  Most of us, except Dr. Allen and Bubba Cleaver, are either retired, virtually retired, or just plain tired.  Thus, it didn’t take long before the acts of volunteering replaced the conversation about the poor-played Monday Night football game.  So, while we look ahead to the home-game with New Orleans, we will sprinkle in a few words  about what to do/not to do in retirement. DR. CHARLES ALLEN:   Charles is still managing and owning a well-established, patient-oriented dental practice.  Somehow, he has eliminated the fear that most people associate with dentists.  He is gentle, painless, and teaches his patients about good dental hygiene and prevention. . . Charles is “befuddled” by it all, especially the play of the Chiefs. . . CHIEFS BY 3. PAUL BOOKER:  Paul teaches math each summer at Freedom School.  In his working years, Paul was a solid resource for children in the Kansas City, Mo., School District.  His wife, Carolyn, was one of the founding administrators for the local Freedom School movement, along with Dwayne Crompton. . . Turn Out The Lights on the Chiefs. . . NEW ORLEANS BY 7. CARL CLARK:  Carl says he has “no problem” as a retiree. . .Carl is one of the fortunate ones, having retired from Colgate with a good retirement plan. . . When he is not guarding the children near the schools, he is doing something positive for the Ivanhoe Club and at times, with the Kiwanis. . .The Chiefs will find another way to self-destruct...that’s why he is picking  NEW ORLEANS BY 7. BUBBA CLEAVER:  Just won his third term as a U.S. Congressman by a landslide.. . . Everyone should see him interact with his grandchildren. . . Cleaver has no plans or room for retirement. . . People are talking again about Presidential appointments. . . Not likely. . .He can’t talk any more about the Chiefs. . . NEW ORLEANS BY 10. IKE GARDNER:  Ike is succinct about his volunteering.  He candidly reflects that he worked two jobs for his family and he ain’t doing nothing else, period.  However, his lovely wife, Lura, Veterans Administration Hospital retiree, continues to volunteer at the City Union Mission. . . Ike does acknowledge and welcome the “new Chiefs” and stated the they are “on the way but haven’t quite arrived yet”. . . but not enough to pick the Chiefs this week. . .NEW ORLEANS BY 10 LLOYD GREENFIELD:   Lloyd looks out for the cultural opportunities for his entire community. . . In fact, the Monday Niters will be his guest at the production of “Brewster’s Place” in early December. . . a pearl of a guy...but is not very nice when it comes to the Chiefs. . . Says the Chiefs can’t play 60 minutes of football. . . thus, NEW ORLEANS BY 5 OLLIE HUBBARD:  No doubt about it, Lincoln University is high on Ollie’s list. . . Recently, he sold more tickets than anybody at the recent Lincoln fundraiser. . . Hounds you at 5:30 a.m. . . Also has high hopes for Obama. . . and now he is liking the Chiefs a little bit. . . CHIEFS BY 3 JIM NUNNELLY:  Not quite retired but in the Social Security line. . . has volunteered substantial time to over 50 organizations. . . will spend his retirement launching a consultant business, called “Temporary Executive Services”. . . doesn’t think the Chiefs are temporary. . .CHIEFS BY 7. ED WEST:  Ed got over with his retirement from AT and T. . . Ed is not exactly lazy but spends a lot of time, repairing and setting up computers for Kansas City home-owners. . .loves his wife, Celeste....she volunteers for senior citizens. . .a likeable family. . .but they don’t like the Chiefs. . . Ed says “they CAN’T beat the SAINTS”. . .NEW ORLEANS BY 6

All of a sudden, the Chiefs went from a “last place” team to a “team in the process of re-building”.  And for the record, Larry Johnson better watch out.

frames.text: The Bible, literature, television and everyday life are full of examples of how the unexpected victor rises, in spite of the odds. Well, that theme is appropriate for the youthful Chiefs as they take on the long-respected Indianapolis Colts.  Yea, we know about the older, more war-like “Philistines”.  There’s Manning  and his passing partner, Reggie Wayne. And then on Kansas City’s side, there are the “Kids R Us”. And in “David and Goliath” fashion, these two teams will meet on Sunday, at noon, in Indianapolis.  And like David, the Chiefs only have a sling shot, and a bag of five stones to throw at last year’s AFC champion. Those five stones are Hali, McCluster, Johnson, Charles, and Jones. It begs the question....can the Chiefs (fresh off a bye week) beat the Colts (fresh off a butt-kicking from Jacksonville)?  The answer is “yes they can”.  But, is it realistic? Yes! But, is likely? NO! And the Monday Niters line up just like those who predicted that Goliath would destroy the little kid, named David. Let’s look in and see what these “haters” think about Sunday’s game. THE VENERABLE DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Doc is truly a bible reader.  He knows that the odds are against the Chiefs’ “kids”  But, he also knows that everyone thought that Goliath would destroy David.  Doc says repeatedly that the Chiefs are better than most people think.  Not a hater at all.  CHIEFS by 10. THE APOSTLE PAUL BOOKER: Booker has consistently “hated on” the Chiefs.  And you can’t blame him for the Chiefs have been “shaky”, as all of us were when we were young. But, Booker says the “impossible” will never happen in Peyton’s Place.  Thus, he sees Goliath as the winner, on Sunday.  COLTS by 14 THE COOL CARL CLARK. . . Carl is not a hater and he is not a loyalist, either.  He’s on the fence a lot, often going with and against the Chiefs. Yet, he seems open to the possibility that the Chiefs may be a developing team that has not played a tough team yet. The Colts are that “tough” team. COLTS by 14 CONGRESSMAN “REV” CLEAVER: Definitely on the campaign trails these days, hoping to be re-elected to the United States Congress. In fact, he created a “preaching songbirds” program that will feature local ministers who sing to their congregations, as well as preach.  So forgive him if he fails to think clearly about the Chiefs and their new rise to prominence.  He’s been too busy campaigning and has allowed Ike and Booker to over-influence his thinking. He says the Chiefs are better, but not going to have a chance in Peyton Place. COLTS by 10. IKE “PAW-PAW” GARDNER: A Chiefs “hater” from way back.  While intelligent, Ike just doesn’t see the light.  Without even thinking it through, he says the Chiefs are leading the NFL’s weakest division. He says the only way the Chiefs can win on Sunday is for the Colts to forfeit the game. Whew! He adds the Chiefs have too many “kids” on their 3-0 team. Regretfully he is taking GOLIATH AND THE COLTS by 17. USUALLY LOYAL LLOYD GREENFIELD: Lloyd has been talk to Ikd and that Booker a lot lately, indicating that he is wavering in his belief about the Chiefs.  Usually, he is fearlessly backing the Chiefs.  But, like the Goliath crowd, he is changing his vote this time and going with the Colts. He believes the Chiefs “are still in their infancy” and cannot beat the Chiefs, at this time. COLTS by 6 OLLIE “CNN” HUBBARD: Any kind of news is Ollie’s business, whether true or untrue. And he thinks there will be “good news”, coming out of Indianapolis on Sunday.  As a member of Ebenezer AME Church, Ollie believes the Chiefs will sink a stone into the “forehead” of the Colts. A former hater, Ollie is now a believer/loyalist. CHIEFS by 3. JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY:  Always supporting the youngsters.  He feels the Chiefs are re-tooled and have new skills, at every position i.e. running back, defensive line, linebackers, secondary, and even the offensive line and special teams. If there is a weakness, it is the “forced bye week” that came when the Chiefs were “rising fast”. Currently, the only undefeated team, the Chiefs will use their “rocks” wisely and overcome the “sluggish” Colts.  Face it yall, Goliath and the Colts are getting older and slower and showing signs of demise.  CHIEFS by 3. ED “THE GEE” WEST: Ed is one of the few “senior citizens” who always packs his i-phone and laptop computer wherever he goes.  And he settles many an argument by just speaking into his phone.  His quiet demeanor serves him well for he usually goes with the facts and never allows the “haters” to get to him. Though he knows the Chiefs can throw running backs at the Colts all day Sunday.  And he knows that the Chiefs are vastly improved over years past.  But, he thinks the Chiefs don’t have enough to beat the Colts. COLTS all the way. ERIC “ERICA’S DAD” WESSON: Eric has not drank the Chiefs’ kool aid yet. Yes they look good defensively in a lot of areas. He feels they have not been tested yet. San Diego is one dimensional  without their work horse running back LaDainian Tomlinson who they let go for some unknown reason. If I were the owner I would fire everyone who had something to do with that deal. Then they beat “no diminsional” Cleveland Browns and San Francisco. payton Manning in the man inspite of several losses early in the season. Once they start rolling they may win 12 games in a row including Sunday’s slacking of the Chiefs by 9. Final Note: Everyone knows there is always a chance for the underdog.  Many of us have prevailed, when all the odds were totally not in our favor.  And that will be the motivation that the Chiefs will take into Indianapolis, Sunday.  Clearly, we are living in “changing times”.  Who would have thought we would ever have a black man in the White House?  And likewise, who would have thought the Chiefs would be undefeated and positioning themselves to become a contender? Those of you who line up with the “haters”, read First Samuel, Chapter 17, verse 49. Enough said.

Be Careful And Cautious, With Those Chiefs

frames.text: Wow!  The New Orleans Saints are 2-0. So are seven other NFL teams.  One of them is the Kansas City Chiefs. But, the Saints’ 2-0 is different than the Chiefs 2-0.   In our minds, the Saints will go on to capture the playoffs, if not repeat as World Champions. Whereas, our Chiefs. . . well, we ain’t sure just what will happen to them.   For those of us over 50, we have been down this road before.  Same stuff, a different year.  And the haters, among us, say it is about to end, this weekend at Arrowhead.  That’s when the Chiefs will face San Francisco, the same team that the Saints just beat this past Monday night.   Bottom line, most of us are basking in delight because we remember last year, when we were 0-2, at this time.   So, let’s all toast the Chiefs and their defense for making us “cautiously happy” with their play, thus far.  But, now let’s turn to the fella’s and see what they think about the Chiefs’ chances against the 49rs. THE VENERABLE DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Doc is skeptical about the quarterback situation with the Chiefs.  He once bought a Cassel t-shirt but left it home and refused to wear it.  Look like he was right because the Chiefs could have won, without Cassel.   Doc says it was the defense, led by Derrick Johnson, that was the difference.  But. unlike the haters, Doc says the CHIEFS will win Sunday. THE APOSTLE PA-UL BOOKER: He is the Executive Vice President of the Chiefs Haters.  And we don’t know where Paul started to go wrong. Many think he is overly influenced by another hater in the Monday Niters.   But, the saintly Paul says that SAN FRANCISCO will win on Sunday, ending the Chiefs good beginning.  He calls it the “Singletary Factor”, citing the 49rs’ head coach as the difference-maker. THE COOL CARL CLARK: Like Doc, Carl is not impressed with Cassel, at all. However, he recognizes that both teams are better, this year, even though the Chiefs are weakly, overall.  Carl, not quite a hater, did select SAN FRANCISCO, to beat the Chiefs. At least by a field goal.  Maybe, Carl is being inducted into the Haters Hall Of Fame. ??? CONGRESSMAN EMANUEL CLEAVER: Steady on the campaign trail, it is fun to watch him take a break from Washington stuff.   In fact, he is slated to become Chairman of the Legislative Black Caucus in Washington, assuming he is re-elected.  That will give him even more access to the President and White House.  Go, Cleaver, go.   Obviously, he is doing fine representing Kansas City in Washington. But, the Congressman has allowed the haters to get to him.  He really believes the Chiefs will be “Gored” to death, citing the slashing running back from the Niners, Frank Gored.  Apparently, Ike and that Booker have gotten to Rev. . . he says SAN FRANCISCO BY 10. FOREVER CANTA-NKEROUS IKE GARDNER: Last week, we observed Ike’s being nice to a certain group of employees at a local restaurant.  They secretly know I am right about his “porcupine-like” personality.  In fact, he has chosen to sit with only one other person, further distancing himself from his old friends.  To further this distance, Ike says that Haley and Cassel are “severe disabilities” and must be dealt with, some kinda way.  That leaves him no hope for the Chiefs this week. . .SAN FRANCISCO BY 13. THE LOYALIST, LLOYD GREENFIELD: Lloyd tries to see hope in whatever he does. Being a part-time thespian, he can find positive, sometimes amid all hopelessness. And he needs it to for there are “haters” in this group.   However vocal the detractors are, Lloyd continues his support for the Chiefs. Specifically, he finds the running backs, Charles and Jones, as promising. Unlike the haters, Lloyd “gets it”. CHIEFS, all the way. THE CNN OF KANSAS CITY, OLLIE HUBBARD: Now, Ollie believes that the Chiefs are going “up, up and away”.  Though he didn’t say where they were going, we assume he means the Chiefs will continue to win. However, we must remember that Ollie is a former hater and can’t be totally believed, right away.   When asked by how much, he proudly screams, CHIEFS BY 18.   Is he right?  Maybe, maybe not.   Now, back to CNN. JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY: I have been friends with the Monday Niters for over forty years and this year, we will celebrate 40 years of uninterrupted friendship.  But, along the way, we have developed into a “two-party” system.  Some of us believe in the Chiefs, no matter what and there are those who DON’T believe in the Chiefs, no matter what. As for me, the Chiefs will have to stop San Francisco’s Smith-to-Davis connection.  And with Kansas City’s weak secondary, one can see why we loyalists ought to be concerned.   In spite of this weakness, the return game and defense will be enough for the Chiefs to advance to 3-0. . .CHIEFS, ALL THE WAY. EASY ED WEST: Ed is a computer geek.  In fact, he spent all of Monday night, player computer scrabble with his son, Damon (who is in California).  But Ed is perceptive, too.   He has seen the Arrowhead crowd make a difference and he is calling on their help to make the Chiefs an early contender.  But for Sunday, Ed has shifted over to the haters, after seeing San Francisco against the Super Bowl Champions Saints. SAN FRANCISCO BY A LOT. Final Note: Too bad the Chiefs have let us down so many times before.  And unfortunately, we think of the Chiefs as losers, rather than victors.   But, whatever we do, we cannot allow these “tea-party like” haters predict and manage our future.   Clearly, the Chiefs are not New Orleans; but they are 2-0.  That makes them equal to the Saints and it is our perception of them that will dictate our expectations of them.   Dr. Allen, Lloyd, even Ollie, and I are aiming and expecting high.  While that Booker, Carl, Cleaver, Cantankerous Ike, and Ed West are usually right, the haters are not omnipotent and are wrong this time..  Let’s see, let’s see.

THE CNN OF KANSAS CITY, OLLIE HUBBARD: Now, Ollie believes that the Chiefs are going “up, up and away”.  Though he didn’t say where they were going, we assume he means the Chiefs will continue to win. However, we must remember that Ollie is a former hater and can’t be totally believed, right away.
When asked by how much, he proudly screams, CHIEFS BY 18.
Is he right?  Maybe, maybe not.
Now, back to CNN.
JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY: I have been friends with the Monday Niters for over forty years and this year, we will celebrate 40 years of uninterrupted friendship.
But, along the way, we have developed into a “two-party” system.  Some of us believe in the Chiefs, no matter what and there are those who DON’T believe in the Chiefs, no matter what.
As for me, the Chiefs will have to stop San Francisco’s Smith-to-Davis connection.  And with Kansas City’s weak secondary, one can see why we loyalists ought to be concerned.
In spite of this weakness, the return game and defense will be enough for the Chiefs to advance to 3-0. . .CHIEFS, ALL THE WAY.
EASY ED WEST: Ed is a computer geek.  In fact, he spent all of Monday night, player computer scrabble with his son, Damon (who is in California).  But Ed is perceptive, too.
He has seen the Arrowhead crowd make a difference and he is calling on their help to make the Chiefs an early contender.
But for Sunday, Ed has shifted over to the haters, after seeing San Francisco against the Super Bowl Champions Saints. SAN FRANCISCO BY A LOT.
Final Note: Too bad the Chiefs have let us down so many times before.  And unfortunately, we think of the Chiefs as losers, rather than victors.
But, whatever we do, we cannot allow these “tea-party like” haters predict and manage our future.
Clearly, the Chiefs are not New Orleans; but they are 2-0.  That makes them equal to the Saints and it is our perception of them that will dictate our expectations of them.
Dr. Allen, Lloyd, even Ollie, and I are aiming and expecting high.  While that Booker, Carl, Cleaver, Cantankerous Ike, and Ed West are usually right, the haters are not omnipotent and are wrong this time..
Let’s see, let’s see.
