frames.text: Ike Gardner is definitely one of a kind. We, in the Monday Niters, risk our emotional lives, each Monday night of the football season. That’s because Ike is cantankerous, arrogant, and one-wayward.  Of course, some of this “fearless candor” can be explained because Ike is/was an only child.  Spending most of his 79 years here, Ike is not a stranger at all. Best known as an educator/administrator, Ike was at the forefront of school desegregation issues, back in the early seventies. There, his candid ways saved the School District from courting catastrophe. He was not diplomatic at all...and thus, we still have some local conrol over our educational system.  In spite of this cantankerousness, Ike is well-respected in our football club. Dr. Allen and Ron Walton refer to him as a “friend for life”. Even though his rough-sounding baritone voice can be heard over everyone, he is well worth listening to. Ike rants and rages his opinion, on anyone who will listen. Just this past Monday, Congressman Cleaver called Ike from Washington, just to check on his behavior. Ike talked Rev.’s head off, going on and on about the Chiefs. Rev actually hung up and Ike didn’t even notice. He just kept on “Ikeing” with fearless candor, leaving the rest of us speechless. But, we must seriously consider what Ike says about the Chiefs and their Chiefs’ 5-0 start. Considering the weak schedule, Ike candidly warns us that there are still eleven games to play in 2013. And even though he is voting for the Chiefs to win against Oakland, he is nonetheless cautious about the Chiefs’ mediocrity. Oakland’s newly-found quarterback, Terrell Pryor, will test the Chiefs’ highly-rated defense. Listen to Ol’ Ike and his candor. Enough of Uncle Cantank. . . now to the rest of us and our thoughts on the Chiefs and other things. Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still reminding us about Alzheimer’s disease. Particularly, he advises care-givers that there is no cure for this awful, life-changing disease. However, he does see a great prognosis for the Chiefs and their momentum. . .Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: He’s happy with the Chiefs’ progress and believes the defense will score often against the Raiders. . . Chiefs by 7 Carl Clark: Carl, on the other hand, believes the Chiefs are bound to lose, sometimes. And he thinks it will be Sunday, out at Arrowhead. Raiders by 7 Lloyd Greenfield: Everyone is commenting on Lloyd’s interest in total community education. Involving everyone in a child’s education is his strong view. Also, he is relentless about the Chiefs and the crowd. . . Chiefs by 3 Ollie Hubbard: Every now and then, Ollie gets out and about. And all the guys were elated to interact with him over dinner (that he didn’t cook or supervise). . . Chiefs by 7 Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He likes the Chiefs’ mental health. They are not breaking down, like they used to, last year. The Chiefs’ defense is among the leagues best, especially the front line and linebackers. Look for some errors but overall this is all. .. Chiefs by 10 Ed West:   Ed once managed the office of Citizens’ Complaints for the Police Department. Thus, he knows all about the need for local control. Leave it like it is, he shouts. Leadership is encouraging, even for the Chiefs. . . winning by 10

frames.text: Editor, THE CALL: Each week during football season, I look forward to reading the “Monday Niters” predictions and the commentary by Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly. Mr. Nunnelly’s commentary in a recent “CALL” issue was particularly interesting as he told a little about each man in the “Monday Nite Footballers group.” Nunnelly is an excellent writer. He knows how to make words on a page come alive. Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men. In a recent  write-up, Nunnelly described these grandfathers of the group from Allen to West as: extraordinary, fantastic, effective, proud, steadfast, remarkable, complete, and encouraging. For what more could one ask? Monday Niters, “Keep on keeping on.” BRAVO!!.  Terry Strother Burlington, Iowa

frames.text: Mila Banks threw her own 100th birthday party, over at the Marriott at 45th and Main last Sunday. About 400  former students, fellow educators, and Christian friends stood in line to congratulate such a remarkable woman. And at the dinner party, we, Monday Niters and wives attended and, were represented by cantankerous Ike Gardner. It was Ike’s idea to make “Ms.  Banks” an honorary Monday Niter. That’s because she is a loyal reader and a good friend to so many of us. So, Ike presented her with a trophy and told that crowd that she will be making her Chiefs’ predictions, right along side ours. But last Monday night  Gen Greenfield prepared a dinner of fresh sweet potatoes and freshly fried fish and a phenomenal salad. Who could argue about anything, with a meal like that in front of you? So the Monday Niters, along with the Go-Along group spent the entire night, talking about how African Americans have been failed by various educational ploys. Here is how some of the conversation went. After that, we will give our predictions on the Buffalo-Chiefs game, coming up Sunday in Buffalo. Ms. Banks will make her prediction, as well. Here goes: There was a time in Kansas City’s history when students coming from the Deep South were routinely put back a grade.  Also, during segregation days, black children from Independence, Excelsior Springs and Pleasant Hill were bussed into the Kansas City Mo., School District. Well into the sixties, there were still one-room schools in the state of  Georgia. In the Bootheel of Southeast Missouri, black students were bussed up to 60 miles each day to attend school. Because cotton was “king”, black kids went to school in “split sessions” i.e. their school year was interrupted to allow for the picking and chopping of cotton.  Ms. Banks attended school in Mount Vernon, about 46 miles west of Springfield, Mo. Because of its erudite faculty, Lincoln High school was rated highly nationwide. Earning college credit while in high school is not a new thing. This was done in the sixties through such great educators like Jeremiah Cameron, Neal Herrford and Chester Anderson. Dr. Charles Allen attended Sumner Elementary and Ike, Carl and Lloyd attended, Wendell Phillips way back in the thirties and forties. Ed West attended school in Osawatomie, Kansas and Jim Nunnelly attended segregated schools in Columbia, Mo. Ms. Banks received unexpected help with her tuition to Lincoln university, way back in the thirties. Today, educating black kids is still an issue in Kansas City.Students who want to leave the unaccredited Kansas City, Mo., School District to attend a nearby accredited school district, are met with the problem of who is to pay for all of this.....the more things change, the more they stay the same. Not so for the Chiefs....they will be 9-0 at the end of the day, Sunday. Here are our thoughts about the Chiefs: Mila  Lewis Banks: Chiefs by 10 Dr. Charles Allen: Chiefs by 10 Paul Booker: Chiefs by 3 Carl Clark: Buffalo by 3 Bubba Cleaver: Chiefs by 7 Ike Gardner: Buffalo by 3 Lloyd Greenfield: Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs by 10 Jim  “GrandDad”  Nunnelly: Chiefs by 2 Ed West: Chiefs by 10 Joe Webster: Chiefs by 6 Rick Davis: Chiefs by 10 Willie Humphrey: Chiefs by 7 Paul Knight: Chiefs by 11 Marshall Robinson: Chiefs by 9 Mike McNeil: Chiefs by 12 Sander Martin: Chiefs by 14

Ms. Banks attended school in Mount Vernon, about 46 miles west of Springfield, Mo. Because of its erudite faculty, Lincoln High school was rated highly nationwide.
Earning college credit while in high school is not a new thing. This was done in the sixties through such great educators like Jeremiah Cameron, Neal Herrford and Chester Anderson.
Dr. Charles Allen attended Sumner Elementary and Ike, Carl and Lloyd attended, Wendell Phillips way back in the thirties and forties. Ed West attended school in Osawatomie, Kansas and Jim Nunnelly attended segregated schools in Columbia, Mo.
Ms. Banks received unexpected help with her tuition to Lincoln university, way back in the thirties.
Today, educating black kids is still an issue in Kansas City.Students who want to leave the unaccredited Kansas City, Mo., School District to attend a nearby accredited school district, are met with the problem of who is to pay for all of this.....the more things change, the more they stay the same.

frames.text: Amid all the opulent commercials, the teams on the field were not expected to be in Tampa Sunday.  Oh yea, all of you AFC fans ere thinking that New England would rise again.  And those New Yorkers thought that the Giants would represent the NFC and return to the most luxurious Sunday of the year.   And some of you thought that Tony Dungy would re-take his Colts, before he retired with his best-selling book proceeds. Well, we were all wrong and we now have (Mike) Tomlin and the Steelers versus Kurt Warner and the Cardinals. And the only thing they have in common is that neither was supposed to be in Super Bowl 43.   Pittsburgh, under its black, second-year coach, has come to be known for its awesome defense. And according to Cleaver, Ike, Carl, and Lloyd, Pittsburgh will slaughter Arizona.   But, some of us will remember Kurt Warner, who conducted the “Greatest Show On Turf”.  He was the pass-happy quarterback under the (Dick) Vermeil-led St. Louis Rams (who went on to the Super Bowl).  So it will an “Arm and Hammer” game that will keep us glued to our big screens, at least until the multi-million-dollar commercials begin.  Laugh of the Day:  Chiefs will be in Super Bowl 44, after going undefeated in 2009. And Carl Peterson will be the General Manager of the opposing NFC team and guess who will be the Head Coach?.. Ha Ha Ha! Charles Allen: Pittsburgh by 14.    Experience, experience, experience! Paul Booker:   Pittsburgh by 14.    I’m black and biased...Tomlin goes all the way! Carl Clark:    Pittsburgh by 7.     Defense will win this game! Bubba Cleaver:  Pittsburgh by 14.    Arizona is the biggest fluke in NFL history! Ike Gardner:  Pittsburgh by 7.     Too much defense! frames.text: Matt Cassel is in trouble. He is injured and he will never know if his likely benching is because of that injury or just inept play. It doesn’t matter because “it is what it is”.  He was well on his way to being benched anyway. And we all know it. And the Monday Niters spent half their meeting session, discussing Matt Cassel. But before we share some crushing comments, let’s look into the non-news-making aspects of this week’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.  Here are some interesting and provocative facts you should know before watching Sunday’s game in Tampa Bay. First, Jamaal Charles is first in the NFL in rushing (no surprise). Justin Huston, Chiefs’ defensive standout is tied for third in quarterback sacks. Tampa Bay’s starting quarterback is Josh Freeman, a graduate of Grandview High school.  Tampa Bay beat the Oakland Raiders in the Super Bowl, just after the 2002 regular season. Bo Jackson refused to play for Tampa Bay, even though he was the first round draft choice. Doug Williams, first African American to quarterback a Super Bowl, was also a first-round pick for Tampa Bay. In 1978, Trent Green, Chiefs quarterback under Dick Vermeil, also suffered a season-ending concussion. And that brings us back to Matt Cassel’s, boo-producing injury, last Sunday against Baltimore.  Here’s what the Monday Niters remarked, along with their predictions for the must-win game against Tampa Bay. Dr. Charles Allen: Believes that if Eric Winston had been doing his job, Cassel wouldn’t have gotten hurt in the first place. Case of sour grapes. Dr. Allen also foresees a coaching change in the near future. Oh?       Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: believes that Matt Cassel was just looking for a way to sit down and take a 60-million dollar rest break...and thereby avoid a lot of bad press. However, Booker says that the hometown boy, Josh Freeman, has no respect for his hometown team. . .thus. . .Tampa Bay by 7 Carl Clark: is truly sorry that Cassel had to get hurt. So he blames the coaches for not taking Cassel out of the game in the first place. Either way, the Chiefs will give the fans “the same old Mitt, warmed over”. . . Tampa Bay by 10 Congressman Emanuel Cleaver: Is busy campaigning. But he did take time out to meet with a few sports fans last Sunday, after the Baltimore game. He spoke candidly about his new-found status in Washington, after having become the chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus. Being a part of a privileged few, he talks weekly with President Obama and goes all over the country in his behalf. But when it comes to the Chiefs, he is embarrassed by their sub-mediocre play. But still stays faithful. . .Chiefs by 7 Ike Gardner: Is nearly 95  years old and has been a Chiefs’ season ticket holder, longer than Winston has been alive. Saying forcefully, he has never witnessed Kansas City fans booing any injured player.  But toward this Sunday’s game, Ike says the Chiefs have talent but have incompetent coaches. . .thus, Tampa Bay by 12 Lloyd Greenfield: Is mad at Eric Winston, recently acquired offensive lineman. Lloyd says he’s been going out to the games for years and he thinks it is unjust and out of place for a player (Winston) to make such a comment. As for this Sunday, Lloyd is afraid they are killing Jamaal Charles, by running him so often and under such impossible circumstances.....but he still remains hopeful. . .Chiefs by 3 Ollie Hubbard:  doesn’t believe that crowd was cheering AGAINST Matt Cassel but they were cheering FOR Brady Quinn. Nonetheless, the fact remains, the Chiefs are lacking in quarterback play. That makes Ollie get down on his knees at Ebenezer and pray. . .Chiefs by 3 Jim Nunnelly: thinks that all the national media coverage is severely overblown and highly sensationalized. Worthless and idle chatter, allowing a newbie like Winston to get some press. The real issue is that Matt Cassel has not played well enough to win. Huston, Johnson, Hali, Charles, Berry again spectacular. . .Chiefs by 6 Ed West: Believes the offense will finally catch up with the defense, especially with a new quarterback. He strongly feels that Cassel was “put” in a bad situation because of horrible coaching (Ed may have something)....nonetheless.....Chiefs by 3 Eric “Amanda, Bri, and Erica’s Dad” Wesson: Asks the question, Does Clark Hunt ever think, in the back of his mind, “Am I’m paying this guy to throw complete passes to the other team. Throw the passes to the guys in the red uniforms you dummy.” .... Chiefs by 3 in overtime

SPT- Monday Niters.indd
If you are up till 9, on Thursday nights, no doubt you have become addicted to the tv drama series, called “Scandal”. It stars Kerry Washington, a black female who operates in and about Washington and all the mess.
However, she is both part of and solution to all the drama, surrounding those who seek and own world power. This chick is bad, yall. She has total access to the President and yet flaunts her courage, wherever and whenever someone needs it. The name “Scandal” is appropriate for the series but more appropriate for the Kansas City Chiefs. Their play, their choices, and all involved are just “scandalous”.
There is no hope to put any hope on. We will get off the fiscal cliff, faster than the Chiefs will win another ball game. Winning only two games out of thirteen, many predict this will be the worst team, ever in the fifty year franchise history. They just can’t find any luck, at all.
Speaking of Luck, there will be some Luck, coming to Arrowhead Sunday. No, not the kind that brings good fortune. Not the kind we wish for at the casinos. His name is Andrew Luck, He is the rookie quarterback of the rising Indianapolis Colts. They chose him in the first round last year and he’s been playing ever since. Unlike the Chiefs, the Colts are building experience, under their youthful quarterback. And they have become contenders for the 2012 playoffs, in the process. This Luck will charm and harm the Chiefs, running and passing and directing. Even dazzling at times, demonstrating to the Chiefs’ fan, the way it is “supposed to be”. And when the game is over, the tv commentators won’t even mention the Chiefs...for it will all be about the Colts and their Luck. And as Booker often states, there will be no joy at Arrowhead. And here is what the rest of the Monday Niters think:
Dr. Charles Allen: My own hopes and desires. Chiefs by 3
Paul Booker: The Colts will ride the Chiefs  plum out of town. Colts by 21
Carl Clark: Not gonna get to Luck.                    Colts by 14
Bubba Cleaver: Winning is habit forming. But Chiefs are proving that cliche wrong. Colts by 14
Ike Gardner:  All the Luck that the Chiefs will get will be bad. Colts by 20
Lloyd Greenfield:  To those  much is given, much is expected. Colts by 14
Ollie Hubbard:  Chiefs can’t ride horses. Colts by 3
Jim Nunnelly:  Luck is better than money. Colts by 30
Ed West:   Luck is gonna run out on them       Colts by 20
Scandal, Luck, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Marvin Gaye is best known for his smash hit song, “Let’s Get It On”. But my favorite, Marvin Gaye song is “Inner City Blues”. In this seventies song, Marvin highlights what it’s like to be an outsider and a non-participant in the American dream. In fact, at one point in the song he screams. . . “makes me want to holler and throw up both my hands”.  Well, given the last few seasons, the Chiefs have sure made a lot of fans “holler and throw up both hands. But, there is a new sheriff and deputies in town and let’s just wait and see what if we can lower our collective hands. Okay, it was important for me to say that first. Speaking of importance, the Monday Niters were special guests of the Kansas City Chiefs this past Tuesday. Yes, the Chiefs treated us like we were royalty up at their training camp in St. Joseph.  They gave us special parking passes, covered and cool sideline seating, lots of beverages, and a ton of material. . . all to emphasize that the 2012 Chiefs are no longer alive. They are dead. And in their place are notables like a new quarterback, Alex Smith and a first-picked, first-round offensive lineman named Eric Fisher. The new coach, Andy Reid, walked around the field like he had “star-trek” hope for these new, improved Chiefs. Joining from the past are the exciting Jamaal Charles, at running back and Dwayne Bowe, acrobatic receiver. This mix of old and new will get its first opportunity-to-impress tonight, against the New Orleans Saints, in a doesn’t-count, preseason game. But it does count for the Chiefs. If the Chiefs should lose, the fans will “holler” louder than before. And the renewed promise of a “new day” will slipper into the usual “hang-ups, let-downs, bad breaks, and set-backs”. They gave us special parking passes, covered and cool sideline seating, lots of beverages, and a ton of material. . . all to emphasize that the 2012 Chiefs are no longer alive. They are dead. The new coach, Andy Reid, walked around the field like he had “star-trek” hope for these new, improved Chiefs. Joining from the past are the exciting Jamaal Charles, at running back and Dwayne Bowe, acrobatic receiver. And of course, there will be a designated player, appointed to tell the fans why we should believe that the Chiefs still deserve our support and that they “will” be better than last year’s 2-14 record. But, oh if they win!

The “holler” will be converted into “screaming for joy”. The hang-ups will be reduced. The let-downs will be lifted up. The bad breaks will be forgiven. And the set-backs will be forgotten. And we will look forward to the regular season, with “red colors” draped all over us.

But, like a line in Marvin Gaye’s song says, “only God knows where the Chiefs are headed”.

frames.text: Bright Lights, Big City And The 9-1 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Bright Lights, Big City And The 9-1 Chiefs

frames.text: Do you remember that old time blues song, “Bright Lights, Big City”? Well, this was a song that was sung by a man from a small town, who was crying about his girlfriend, who had gone to the “big city” and no longer needed or loved him. In fact, the song says….”bright lights and big city, they went to my baby’s head”. And that’s exactly what happened to the Chiefs last Sunday night. All the hype and national headlines just messed the Chiefs up. Here’s a 2-14 team last year, hearing daily how they lost all last year and now are on top of the entire National Football League and undefeated on top of that.  That was just too much for the Chiefs to handle.  They got caught up in the “bright lights” and lost badly to Denver. Now, let’s hope they return to normal and beat the 4-6 San Diego Chargers. Now, that the lights have been turned off, let’s see if they can win number 10 out at Arrowhead Sunday. But big praise should go to Ike Gardner and Carl Clark, for seeing through all the hype, They knew the Chiefs would fold, with the eyes of the world on them. So, we all had to kiss their rings for seeing through the “offense-less” Chiefs. . So the song, “Bright Lights, Big City” set off a conversation about the singers of the fifties, sixties and seventies. It was remarkable how sharp these old minds were in remembering all the artists of days gone by.  Some of those top names were, Sonny Thompson, Lula Reed, Ruth Brown, Etta James “Annie Had A Baby” by Hank Ballard and the Midnighters, ”I Only Have Eyes For You” by the Flamingoes, Lou Rawls, Johnny Taylor and Sam Cooke all former lead singers from the gospel group, the Soul Stirrers, Fontella Bass, Little Willie John and “Fever”, Ike and Tina Turner,  Jackie Wilson’s “Lonely Teardrops”, Fats Domino and The Dominoes, The Moonglows. and on and on. Before you knew it, we were all drifting back so far…that we either fell asleep or forgot we came to watch a football game and talk about the Chiefs and their first loss.  Then we woke up and remembered that we had to make our predictions. Here’s how we think Sunday’s game will go. Dr. Charles Allen:   Embarrassed, but K.C. will beat the Chargers.Chiefs by 14 Mrs. Mila Lewis Banks: Going to Kansas City, here I come. Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: Phillip will be sent up the Rivers. Chiefs by 10 Carl Clark, Denver exposed K.C’s weaknesses. Chargers by 7 Ike Gardner: Don’t worry about the alligator in the pond down the road. Chargers by 7 When your foot is in the middle of a snake pit. Lloyd Greenfield: K.C. has a debt to pay and they will settle it. Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: Praying for Kansas City, Chiefs by 3 Jim Nunnelly:  I know it’s gonna work out fine (Ike Turner). Chiefs by 17 Ed West: Welcome home to the 12th man (the crowd). Chiefs by 7 City……………………………….Chiefs by 3

frames.text: Chiefs Are Not Pearls. . . More Like Costume Jewelry…

paragraphs.text: Chiefs Are Not Pearls. . . More Like Costume Jewelry…

frames.text: Someone once said that “a pearl is not a pearl, until it comes out of its shell”. That should have become the theme for our Monday night session, down at the Juke House. Congressman Cleaver hosted the event Monday and the evening was full of history lessons. That meant that everyone was cordial to each other (being the first meeting of the season). Then, things turned sour and we began to verbally assault the Chiefs. However before that we spent considerable time, talking about the domestic violence in the NFL, a revered teacher in the Kansas City Public Schools history, and then, we lit in on the Chiefs. First, about the domestic violence. This subject arose because the news media is going crazy, talking about the elevator video showing Ray Rice beating his girlfriend. Under the new NFL policy, he will be suspended for six games and if a second event occurs, he could be banned “for life”. This week the Baltimore Ravens cut Rice’s contract and the NFL suspended him indefinitely. Let’s go on. Secondly, we reminisced. Mainly about the “good old days”, when education was truly our number one priority in Kansas City. Jimmy Ray Hubbard said during a recent visit that at one time “Lincoln High School had more master’s level and PhD teachers than any other school. That’s why the guys, especially Ike, Carl, Ed and Lloyd saluted Dr. Jeremiah Cameron, English teacher at Lincoln in the forties and fifties and sixties. Sadly but understandably, some short-sighted people labeled the late Dr. Cameron as “arrogant”. But always  lauded for his teaching skills and his relentless efforts to fully educate our children. And to Jimmy Ray Hubbard’s point, he had a master’s in English from the University of Chicago and an earned PhD from Michigan State University. Now, this “pearl” is/was definitely out of his shell. In fact, it makes us all nostalgic….wishing for the “good old days”, when the quality of our educational system was never in question.  Lastly, we turned to another “pearl” that is nowhere near “out of the shell”. Yes, we all chimed in our luck-less, lifeless Kansas City Chiefs, After the shellacking they received Sunday by Tennessee, Ed West quickly said the Chiefs may only win two games this year. Booker, who is really happy these days, said the Chiefs are not worth a (four letter word). And we were all uniform in believing that Alex Smith is more like “costume jewelry” than a pearl. And everyone is still wondering why Jamaal Charles remained in his shell, all afternoon. At some point, we all became redundant and as usual, we began to repeat ourselves. So real quickly, the question was asked. . . “how will the Chiefs do against Denver on Sunday”. Well, I’ve never witnessed such laughter in my life. It was like Kat Williams or Kevin Hart had told a funny joke.  Now folks, Denver is saturated with “all kinds of pearls”….Manning, a great offensive line, Vonn Miller, an effective secondaryand on and on. So except for two loyalists, all of us believe the Chiefs will be murdered by the Broncos.  In fact, the mood switched from speaking highly about Dr. Jeremiah Cameron to a relentless cascade of tears for the sad Chiefs. And we left there, with the Chiefs’ pearls, still in their shell…… Dr. Charles Allen. A hope and a prayer. . . . Chiefs by 3 Paul Booker: K.C. cannot tame Denver . . . Denver by 14. Carl Clark: K.C.  has no offensive line . . . Denver by 21. Ike Gardner: Weak corners and an even weaker defensive line . . . Denver by 28. Lloyd Greenfield: No line, no kicker . . . Denver by 14 Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs better perk up . . . Chiefs by 3 Jim Nunnelly:  Not coming out this week . . . Denver by 30         Ed West: K.C. can’t tackle, can’t score . . . Denver by 21 Bubba Cleaver.    2 much Manning 2 manage. . . Denver by 14 Eric Wesson “Erica, E.J. Amanda and Bri’s Dad”:. . . Denver will exploit the middle of the field, the corners, special teams and coaching staff . . . Denver by 28 at least.

frames.text: Peanute Brittle, Melody Lanes And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Peanute Brittle, Melody Lanes And The Chiefs

frames.text: We, Monday Niters, have given up on the Chiefs.  They have been beaten badly by the doormats of the NFL, i.e. Buffalo and Detroit.  What’s more they have lost their only offensive hope through injury. . .Jamal Charles. All they have left now is Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel.  Yes, that’s an appropriate name for Cassel because he is worth only “peanuts” and he is always injured, therefore, “brittle”. So, he is now a  bona fide member of a long line of “broken” Chiefs’ quarterbacks. So, we collectively think the Chiefs will get shocked again Sunday by the San Diego Chargers. The Chargers will strike the Chiefs for with six or seven touchdowns. Speaking of strikes, we talked a lot about old bowling alleys and good bowling athletes. There have been several bowling establishments frequented by African Americans in the ‘60s -- Monarch Lanes, Melody Lanes, King Louie East and even K.C. Bowl in Kansas. And of late, there is a major bowling contingency that now goes to Premier out in Raytown. Just go out there on a Tuesday afternoon and see scores of seniors rolling the ball. And on Fridays and Thursdays, you can find some of the best bowling around. So, in this column, we prefer to talk about bowlers of yesteryears, rather than talk about Peanut Brittle And The Candy Stripers. So now for a walk down Memory Lanes. Dr. Charles Allen: Way back in 1952, Doc was a pin-setter at Sakin’s bowling alley, near Linwood and Troost. In the old days, bowling pins were set manually, and usually by African American youth at white establishments. Though he did not bowl much, he felt unsafe in that job. But not unsafe about the locals. Chiefs by 3 Paul “6902” Booker: Booker believes the there is no way that the Chiefs can beat San Diego. And he has felt that way since he came here in 1966. He does remember Fred Broski’s bowling for dollars. Money or not. San Diego by 40 Carl “Classy” Clark: Believes the Chiefs are just pitiful. But does remember being a league bowler at Melody Lanes in 1965, on a team sponsored by Northwestern Mutual Insurance Company. Not enough insurance for the Chiefs to win, though.  San Diego by 14 Congressman “Bubba” Cleaver: Believes the Chiefs are “out of and out for the season. Wisely, Cleaver has appointed a group to research and honor the black bowlers of the past. This group includes Jauqua Preston, Joe Newsome, Nero Hartridge, Ron Winfrey, Maxine Walker, LaDonna Hendrix, Sam Coleman, Jiles Dunn, Deborah Cheadle Thomas, Joycelyn Burgo, Alex Harris, Willie Henderson Jim Nunnelly and Bill Johnson. An announcement is expected soon on the outcomes. Outcome bad for Chiefs. San Diego by 10 Ike “Spoiled by Niecie’s” Gardner: Ike was pin-setter at a white bowling alley in the ‘50s. As a worker, he had to use the back door to enter. Now, that was a long time ago.  He hated segregation as much as he hates the Chiefs.  San Diego by 35 Lloyd “Loyal Up To A Point” Greenfield: Lloyd is one of the seniors who bowl at Premier on Tuesdays. Bowling a cool 152 average, he is surrounded by seniors who can really bowl and who know a lot about Kansas City’s history. But, this time, Lloyd switches over from the Chiefs. San Diego by 7 Ollie “Breaking New ” Hubbard: Ollie remembers going to parties at the Rhythm Lanes on Troost, way back in the sixties. The teenagers went there for music and refreshments. But, the Chiefs are not refreshing at all and he expects a bolt of lightning to hit the Chiefs. San Diego by 35 Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: started bowling at King Louie East, when Ron Winfrey became the first black to manage a bowling establishment. Hopes to record some of this rich bowling history. But history will be made Sunday when the Charges run up the largest score in NFL history on the Chiefs. San Diego by 50 Ed “Still Mentoring” West: Being brought up in Osawatamie, Kansas, Ed was only permitted to bowl one night a week at the white bowling alley. However, later he joined the St. James bowling league in 1980. Never a true bowler, he feels the Chiefs have no coach, no offense, no defense thus no win. San Diego by 38

And of late, there is a major bowling contingency that now goes to Premier out in Raytown. Just go out there on a Tuesday afternoon and see scores of seniors rolling the ball. And on Fridays and Thursdays, you can find some of the best bowling around. So, in this column, we prefer to talk about bowlers of yesteryears, rather than talk about Peanut Brittle And The Candy Stripers.

So now for a walk down Memory Lanes.

Dr. Charles Allen: Way back in 1952, Doc was a pin-setter at Sakin’s bowling alley, near Linwood and Troost. In the old days, bowling pins were set manually, and usually by African American youth at white establishments. Though he did not bowl much, he felt unsafe in that job. But not unsafe about the locals. Chiefs by 3

Paul “6902” Booker: Booker believes the there is no way that the Chiefs can beat San Diego. And he has felt that way since he came here in 1966. He does remember Fred Broski’s bowling for dollars. Money or not. San Diego by 40

Carl “Classy” Clark: Believes the Chiefs are just pitiful. But does remember being a league bowler at Melody Lanes in 1965, on a team sponsored by Northwestern Mutual Insurance Company. Not enough insurance for the Chiefs to win, though. San Diego by 14

Congressman “Bubba” Cleaver: Believes the Chiefs are “out of and out for the season. Wisely, Cleaver has appointed a group to research and honor the black bowlers of the past. This group includes Jauqua Preston, Joe Newsome, Nero Hartridge, Ron Winfrey, Maxine Walker, LaDonna Hendrix, Sam Coleman, Jiles Dunn, Deborah Cheadle Thomas, Joycelyn Burgo, Alex Harris, Willie Henderson Jim Nunnelly and Bill Johnson. An announcement is expected soon on the outcomes. Outcome bad for Chiefs. San Diego by 10

Ike “Spoiled by Niecie’s” Gardner: Ike was pin-setter at a white bowling alley in the ‘50s. As a worker, he had to use the back door to enter. Now, that was a long time ago. He hated segregation as much as he hates the Chiefs. San Diego by 35

Lloyd “Loyal Up To A Point” Greenfield: Lloyd is one of the seniors who bowl at Premier on Tuesdays. Bowling a cool 152 average, he is surrounded by seniors who can really bowl and who know a lot about Kansas City’s history. But, this time, Lloyd switches over from the Chiefs. San Diego by 7

Ollie “Breaking New ” Hubbard: Ollie remembers going to parties at the Rhythm Lanes on Troost, way back in the sixties. The teenagers went there for music and refreshments. But, the Chiefs are not refreshing at all and he expects a bolt of lightning to hit the Chiefs. San Diego by 35

Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: started bowling at King Louie East, when Ron Winfrey became the first black to manage a bowling establishment. Hopes to record some of this rich bowling history. But history will be made Sunday when the Charges run up the largest score in NFL history on the Chiefs. San Diego by 50

Ed “Still Mentoring” West: Being brought up in Osawatamie, Kansas, Ed was only permitted to bowl one night a week at the white bowling alley. However, later he joined the St. James bowling league in 1980. Never a true bowler, he feels the Chiefs have no coach, no offense, no defense thus no win. San Diego by 38

Spt - Monday Niters 1230

Monday Nite Footballers Predictions

By Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly

Predicting Since 1970

Kansas City Chiefs vs. Cincinatti Bengals

12:00 p.m. KCTV 5

   “Forks In The Road”

 Obviously, this game is it! The Chiefs have come to the fork in the road…either they win or we will all turn our attention and support to Tony Dungy (Indianapolis) and Marvin Lewis (Cincinnati). But if Detroit should happen to beat Pittsburg and Denver wipes out San Diego and the Chiefs beat up on Cincinnati…. then, the Chiefs will make the playoffs. Folks, it is that simple. And complicating matters is the hovering speculation that Vermeil will retire…one way or the other. Clearly, Vermeil is at the fork in the road, too. Win and stay in! Lose and sign up for Medicare! Folks, it is that simple.

 And we, Monday Niters, are facing another kind fork in the road. Monday Night Football, as we know it, is over. ABC will no longer broadcast the perennial ratings-winner. In fact, we all said our goodbyes to Al Michaels and John Madden and reminisced about all the history-making plays witnessed on Monday night television, everywhere. In 1970, we were all younger, quicker, and immature. Now we are older, slower and fall asleep, with no warning. It takes us longer to do EVERYTHING, including selecting our teams. Some of us even have to ask “who’s playing”. The fork in the road for us is that we are just getting old and things are changing, with or without our support. But some things will never change….Ike, Ollie and that Booker will always be haters of the Chiefs. Cleaver, Carl, and Ed West will go with the wind. And faithful, fine people like Lloyd Greenfield and imminent Dr. Allen, will always support the Chiefs, just like on New Year’s Day against North Division champions, Cincinnati. We know the Chiefs will win by at least ten and Vermeil stays in. We never have been at that fork in the road!

 Like each of you, we will have to switch the channel over to ESPN and carry on as usual. Booker, Ollie and Ike will continue to hate the Chiefs. And Ed, Carl and Cleaver will switch up, every now and then. And Dr. Charles Allen, Lloyd Greenfield and I will always support the Chiefs. Wisely, we don’t have to face a fork in the road. We know the way, just like we have always done. And just for the record, we will be looking for the Chiefs to win on New Year’s Day, out at Arrowhead. Chiefs by 10 and Vermeil will be back, again!

Spt- SG Monday Niter

By The Sports Guy

 Some of the members of the infamous Monday Niters, who have been watching Monday Night football together for 34- years, will be featured on the Tailgate show Monday night on Channel 9 before the Chiefs play or get beat by the Tennessee Titans.

 The group has a column that has been featured in THE CALL with their football predictions of Chiefs’ games since 1980 but began with their New Year’s column in 1970.

 They rotate around to each members home for dinner on Monday nights. The Sports Guy has had the opportunity to attend a couple of Monday night games at the home of Jim Nunnelly and recently Ed West. They are all really a great group of guys.

 There is a great deal of wisdom and history in the room and they will even be helping The Sports Guy pass out Christmas baskets to needy families next week, but have to tell you. If you really want to watch a football game and actually hear what is said, don’t go near them on Monday night, you won’t hear a thing.

 Anything that you can think of is a topic of discussion.

 Ike Gardner boasts that he has won the most games overall in the group’s history of course he is immediately challenged by Lloyd Greenfield, Carl Clark and Paul Booker even wakes up to challenge Gardner’s claim that he has won the most games.

 “I want to tell you all something. I am not opposed to the Chiefs as much as some of you all are. You paint the picture that I am always against the Chiefs. I am only against them when they are playing a team that they cannot beat. I have never said that they Chiefs are going to lose all of the time,” said Gardner.

 “See that ole’ fat mouth Nunnelly started that,” Gardner yelled.

 Of course Nunnelly denies doing any such thing.

 Ed West shares the secret of the groups long term success.

 “Our wives deserve most of the credit. They cook for all of us and make their homes presentable for guests. They are very gracious hosts for a bunch of ragga’ muffins,” said West.

  “It is a lot cheaper now to host a game than it was when I first joined the group 25-years ago. Nobody drinks anymore so we don’t have the cost of buying alcohol,” West said.

 There are countless photos of the group through the years and the events that they have attended both in Kansas City and St. Louis when there was a group of Monday Niters there. And there were too many New year’s parties to count.

 There is even a Governor’s Cup trophy that the group competed against St. Louis with.

If you really want to watch a football game and actually hear what is said, don’t go near them on Monday night, you won’t hear a thing.
&hTab;Anything that you can think of is a topic of discussion.
&hTab;Ike Gardner boasts that he has won the most games overall in the group’s history of course he is immediately challenged by Lloyd Greenfield, Carl Clark and Paul Booker even wakes up to challenge Gardner’s claim that he has won the most games.
&hTab;“I want to tell you all something. I am not opposed to the Chiefs as much as some of you all are. You paint the picture that I am always against the Chiefs. I am only against them when they are playing a team that they cannot beat. I have never said that they Chiefs are going to lose all of the time,” said Gardner.
&hTab;“See that ole’ fat mouth Nunnelly started that,” Gardner yelled.
&hTab;Of course Nunnelly denies doing any such thing.
&hTab;Ed West shares the secret of the groups long term success.
&hTab;“Our wives deserve most of the credit. They cook for all of us and make their homes presentable for guests. They are very gracious hosts for a bunch of ragga’ muffins,” said West.
&hTab; “It is a lot cheaper now to host a game than it was when I first joined the group 25-years ago. Nobody drinks anymore so we don’t have the cost of buying alcohol,” West said.
&hTab;There are countless photos of the group through the years and the events that they have attended both in Kansas City and St. Louis when there was a group of Monday Niters there. And there were too many New year’s parties to count.
&hTab;There is even a Governor’s Cup trophy that the group competed against St. Louis with.

frames.text: Carolina Panthers at Kansas City Chiefs 12:00 p.m., KCTV&punctSpace;5 &hTab; &hTab; &hTab;&hTab;             Predictions (Wins In Parenthesis) Chatter, Conversation And Commentary Shame on you, you fair-weather Chiefs' fans. You are joining up with the haters (Ike and Booker).  You are acting like the Chiefs are 0-5, rather than 0-1.  Hey, this is just the first game and while there are things to be fixed, 16 other teams lost, last week-end, as well.  So, let’s not talk as if there are no more opportunities to win. In fact, watching Carolina play on Monday night reminded us all that this was the team that was in last year’s Super Bowl.  They certainly didn't look like they were the 2003 NFC champs.  Further, the Chiefs will again get yet another opportunity to power up its powerful offense and improve its lackluster defense.  And just think, there will be fourteen games after that. Bottom line, we will have plenty of time to see if the Chiefs are for real or if they are just pretenders.  The jury is still out on Gunther and even Al Sanders and yes, even Dick Vermeil. So, let's just wait a while before we write off our beloved Chiefs. We’ve got a tough schedule ahead and we will have to be at our level best.  But, fans, it is only the second game.  Let's be patient. Editor’s Note:  Paul Booker and Ike Gardner were the only two winners in last week’s prediction of the Denver game. Way to go Paul and Ike!

frames.text: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Oakland Raiders 4:00 p.m., KCTV  5 &hTab; &hTab; &hTab;&hTab; MERRY&punctSpace;CHRISTMAS&punctSpace;FROM&punctSpace;THE&punctSpace;MONDAY&punctSpace;NITERS. . . Although the Kansas City Chiefs won’t be participating in the 2004 NFL&punctSpace;playoffs, the&punctSpace;Monday Niters still want to wish its readers and Kansas City a Merry Christmas and a Happy New&punctSpace;Year. Shown are, Paul Booker, Charles Allen, Jim Nunnelly, Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield, and Carl Clark. Not shown are Bubba Cleaver, Ollie Hubbard and Ed West. -- CALL photo by Rex Purefoy Charles Allen&hTab;Chiefs by 14&hTab;Repeat performance Paul Booker       Chiefs by 10&hTab;Larry fell down but he got up Carl Clark&hTab;Chiefs by 7&hTab;Chiefs will plug up the Black Hole Bubba Cleaver&hTab;Chiefs by 14&hTab;Battle of the used-to-be’s; but we be's                                         &hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;better Ike Gardner&hTab;Chiefs by 1&hTab;Stevie Wonder fights Ray Charles Lloyd &hTab;&hTab;Chiefs by 7&hTab;And the beat(ing) goes on! Greenfield&hTab; Ollie Hubbard &hTab;Raiders by 6 &hTab;Raiders will walk the plank again Jim Nunnelly&hTab;Chiefs by 23&hTab;Johnson saves Vermeil's -- (job) Ed West&hTab;&hTab;Raiders by 20&hTab;Reverse psychology, still in effect Chatter, Conversation And Commentary &hTab;When high-powered, highly-paid coaches sign on to become a head coach in the NFL, there are lots of neat little “perks” that find their way into a contract. &hTab;For example, there are additional dollars added, when a team makes the playoffs or avoid a losing season. Well, for the Chiefs, Vermeil and company will not be in the hunt for the playoffs. But, if they win the next two games, that could mean “bigger bucks” for the coaches. For while they would not have had a winning season, it would not be a losing season, either. &hTab;This is just a lesson in the “small print” of these big-time contracts.  Then, too, Vermeil has some making up to do both with the fans and specifically, with Larry Johnson.  This boy can run that ball, equal to or better than Priest Holmes.  And Vermeil, because of some personal issues with Johnson, kept Johnson out of competition, even though he was a high-round, draft choice.  And to see Johnson perform like he has lately, Vermeil has to save face and let Larry run around, through, and  over Oakland.  Look for Larry and the Chiefs to save Dick Vermeil’s -- (job). More important, a full stadium on Christmas Day will help save any threatened decrease in season ticket sales.  On the other hand, the Chiefs should not expect the fans to pay for an increase in ticket prices.  For really, this season has been mediocre, at best.  Chiefs 40, Raiders 17. &hTab;Note: Congressman-elect Cleaver is still homeless in D.C., having failed to locate an apartment on his last trip East.  Ike Gardner and Ed West, fellow Monday Niters and St. James members, are assisting Cleaver by providing contacts.  Cleaver is planning to be  in Washington Tuesday thru Thursday of every week and here in Kansas City Friday through Monday. Cleaver will return to Washington for swearing-in ceremonies on January 4, 2005,  At that time, he hopes to surrender his homelessness card. &hTab;

frames.text: Carl Clark was in the Navy and travelled extensively. That introduction to the world has netted him many friends and benefits. In fact, he earned the nickname “Sweet Pea” because he is generally a likeable guy. Because of that, he is well known across the metropolitan area, especially in social circles. He is the “grand-master of the 6902 Club” and has served as president of the prestigious Ivanhoe Club.  But, his real passion is the safety of children. You can see him any day at Fifty First and Main, caring for the children who have to cross the street to Visitation Catholic school. For doing such a good job and being well-liked, he is known as the “priest of safety”. Since 1995, he has been there on that corner, doing what he feels is his calling....protecting the kids from predators and crazy drivers. But, Carl is best known for his role in the Monday Niters, He is so opinionated that his fellow friends are noting that he is getting more like that Ike Gardner, everyday. Carl, who used to support the Chiefs is now voting against them, week after week. In fact, he said the Chiefs will not win more than five games this season. To his chagrin,the Chiefs have already won four and are looking any day for that fifth victory. .So at his house Monday night, everyone was kidding Carl about the above picture....that shows him holding up the number “five”. Like other doubters, Carl is having to rethink his early predictions and yet he holds to his prediction and says the Chiefs will lose to Tennessee Titans by a field goal..  Except for Ike, his fellow Monday Niters disagree. Let’s now look in and see what the rest of the guys think. Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still concerned about this Alzheimer’s disease. Particularly, he is warning all care-givers that it takes more than “24-7” to look after those, with Alzheimer’s. But he is quite optimistic about the Chiefs, especially the coaching aspect. Thus, he sees Sunday as another victory for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7. PAUL BOOKER:  Interested in all the violence, Booker has high praise for Jackson County. The County has just released a plan to curtail some of the violence and he is elated about that. And he’s happy about the Chiefs being 4-0. He says it is strictly because of those linebackers....Hali, Houston and Johnson. Chiefs by 10 Bubba Cleaver: He is up to his neck in dealing with the government “shutdown” in Washington. He attends every session, hoping for a resolution. . . but there is definitely a war going on in the nation’s capital.. But Cleaver is keeping the faith and still earning national respect, every day. Just like the Chiefs. No doubt about Sunday.  Chiefs by 7. Ike “Out of Control” Gardner: Ike is intelligent, committed but cantankerous as hell. He flatout disagrees with everybody, except his current and past St. James pastors, both Rev. and E-3.  He did say a few nice things about Dontari Poe, the Chiefs defensive nose guard. But, he was Ol’ Ike when it came to the outcome, Tennessee by 3. Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd, unlike painful Ike, is a mild-mannered, thoughtful guy. He feels that educated people are more effective, when they share their talents with lesser educated people. This “team” approach will make the city, better for everyone. Further, he is pleased with the Chiefs’ team play and Jamaal Charles in particular. They will shine again in Tennessee Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: Big Hub is one of Lincoln University’s greatest advocates. If Lincoln is having a fundraiser, Ollie will call you at 3 a.m., to remind you of your “forced” promise to buy a ticket to a Lincoln event. That dedication has earned him many friends. Just like his wisdom in supporting the Chiefs, this Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly:  He is really gung-ho about this mental health and violence stuff. His family is running from him because he is urging them to get involved in this community issue. His grandson, Christian, says his grandfather is all about “liberating mental health”. In fact, he notes a mental uplift in the Chiefs. The special teams are leading the way., including this Sunday. Chiefs by 7 Ed West: He keeps wondering why local  control of the police department keeps coming up. With people leading the board like Alvin Brooks, Ed asks “what’s the problem”? He is asking that about the Chiefs, as well. With special teams scoring points and getting good field position. . . what’s the problem?. . . thus, Chiefs by 10.

frames.text: Long before Kerry Washington became “a Thursday night must-see”, she starred along side Jamie Foxx in the 2004 major flick, “Ray”.  In fact, she played Ray Charles’ wife and stood firm and steady, all through Ray Charles’ ups and downs and yes, even a nasty heroin addiction. We all knew then that Kerry would rise to the top, especially since she possesses the ability to use “all of her” in her acting craft. Eyes. Nose, Forehead. Eyebrows.Facial creases. This woman exudes totality and entirety. Everything about her makes the scene advance. When acting, Kerry rules. Speaking of rules, let’s talk a minute about the Golden Rule. While many think this is a biblical expression, it really came along, long before Christianity. It simply says “do unto others as you would have them do unto you”. Well, the Chiefs will have a chance to do just that against Denver this Sunday. Beaten badly in the “mile-high” city two weeks ago, the Broncos will come riding into Arrowhead, after a horse-whipping from the New England Patriots last Sunday. Yes, Denver jumped out to a 24-0 lead, only to fall to the “totally magic arm” of Tom Brady. Eventually, the Patriots prevailed with a record-breaking comeback, in the second half. The first half, all Denver. The second half, it was all New England. That brings us to the Chiefs and Denver. Both teams are vying for the AFC West and a guarantee of home-field advantage in the playoffs. And really, it’s much more.  Kansas City has to prove that it can “hang” with the best teams, a second time. Against San Diego, the offense finally showed up and the defense went to sleep. frames.text: Marvin Gaye, Matt Cassel,  And Those Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Marvin Gaye, Matt Cassel,
And Those Chiefs

frames.text: Y’all know Marvin Gaye, He was the greatest Motown singer ever. Singing hits like “Heard It Through The Grapevine” and “Let’s Get It On” and “Makes Me Wanna Holler”.  But one of his most unknown songs was entitled, “Ain’t That Peculiar”. It is with this song in mind that we will talk about the Kansas City Chiefs, this week. Many of you know that the Chiefs will be facing the Buffalo Bills, in Buffalo, New York this Sunday. And let’s not forget that Matt Cassel will still  be the starting quarterback for the Chiefs. . . again. This past Monday night, we all met out at the Groove Station, in South Kansas City. It is all part of our “get out and see the City” campaign. We, Monday Niters, have been going to each other’s homes for over forty years and from now on, we will find out what the restaurant cuisine is really like. But, the point is we talked about the Chiefs’ highly-inadequate quarterback, Matt Cassel.  Ain”t it peculiar that Matt Cassel never started a college football game. That’s because he played backup to Matt Leinart and Carson Palmer at USC. Further, ain’t it peculiar that he was not a starter in the NFL, either. He gained fame by backing up New England’s Tom Brady, during an unexpected injury. So it’s begs the question....why in the hell should the Chiefs’ expect any more than a backup game, when Matt Cassel is still starting? Now, that is peculiar. But let’s move on, knowing that the Chiefs will not win unless they replace Matt Cassel. Enough said about that. Back to the Groove Station venue. Ollie hosted us out there because he lives only a few blocks away. That’s Ollie....location, location. And the cuisine was some delicious chicken wings, backed up with a nice sports salad. And the owner shared her story with all the guys. But, we were only interested in talking about the Chiefs’ chances against lowly Buffalo. Except for a couple of us die-hards, everyone picked Buffalo over the Chiefs, especially after that high-school showing against Tony Gonzalez and the Atlanta Falcons. All the guys think that the Chiefs still have a long way to go, before winning. Thus, it is not “peculiar” that they would pick Buffalo over the “Casseled-out” Chiefs. They think that Buffalo’s defense, led by $100 million dollar man, Mario Williams, will maul the Chiefs. Even though Buffalo’s quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick, ain’t no better than Cassel. Now, ain’t that peculiar? Dr. Charles Allen: Sweet revenge from last year Chiefs by 7 Paul Booker: Chiefs are not ready for prime time     Buffalo by 10 Carl Clark:  Chiefs still ain’t ready Buffalo by 7 Bubba Cleaver: Still thinks he’s at the Democratic Convention Chiefs by 7 Ike Gardner: Chiefs need another month  Buffalo by 12 Lloyd Greenfield: Another time, another day Chiefs by 3 Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs gotta do better Buffalo by 12 Jim Nunnelly: Believing in Hali, Johnson, Charles     Chiefs by 3 Ed West: No improvement from last year Buffalo by 10 national convention Eric “Amanda, Bri and Erica’s Dad” Wesson:

paragraphs.text: Interim Superintendent
And The Lowly Chiefs

frames.text: The NFL season is finally here. After a threatened strike, a boatload of free agents, and a new set of feet, the Chiefs will open at Arrowhead on Sunday. And you will see folks going to early morning church services, in order to witness the kickoff game to the 2011 season. And like the tornado that hit Joplin and the hurricane Irene that racked the east coast, the Chiefs have a lot of damage to clean up. You know they released All Pro offensive lineman, Brian Waters. And Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel is ailing, as usual. Then, the Chiefs did not win a single pre-season game, this summer. That all adds up to another questionable season ahead, in spite of the fact the Chiefs made the playoffs last year. In many ways, the Chiefs are like the Kansas City, Mo., School District.  Every year, they come up with a different reason why any kind of success evades them. In fact, Big Bad John Covington balanced the budget but he did absolutely nothing to improve the test scores. He closed a lot of schools but did not open up any new academic trails.  And once again, Booker says it is purely chaotic, down at 1211 McGee. No one knows what to do about it and that’s tragic. As expected each year, the enrollment, the energy and the ebullience decreases.  I suggest that at least the Board ought to hire an Associate Superintendent, whose only job is to monitor the academic progress of our children and keep the community updated on the accreditation status.  This person should be a resident of Kansas City and  have credibility in our community.  This over-reliance on itinerant Superintendents is crazy. And we in this community can change that. We really can. All right, enough of that.  Let’s return to talking about the Cheaps (I mean Chiefs). Ike Gardner and Paul Booker are back at their old habits again. They can’t see the Chiefs beating anybody this year. After all, the Chiefs play New England, San Diego twice, Pittsburg, Minnesota, Indianapolis, and even Detroit. That’s what happens when a non-playoff-calibre teams make the playoffs, They suffer greatly the next year. But Carl Clark, Ollie Hubbard, and of course, Dr. Charles Allen believe the Chiefs will be “up” for the challenge and will win their first game, against Buffalo. So, like the School District, the Chiefs are steadily losing their support....both here and nationally.  What will it take to get it back for both of these also-rans?  It’s simple. Just do SOMETHING right. Anything. Is help on the way? As is our duty, we will monitor the progress and report to you each week.  Just like we have been doing for forty two years now. Whew! Time passes, doesn’t it.  Hint to the District and the Chiefs.

Ike Gardner and Paul Booker are back at their old habits again. They can’t see the Chiefs beating anybody this year. But Carl Clark, Ollie Hubbard, and of course, Dr. Charles Allen believe the Chiefs will be “up” for the challenge and will win their first game, against Buffalo. So, like the School District, the Chiefs are steadily losing their support....both here and nationally.

What will it take to get it back for both of these also-rans?

It’s simple. Just do SOMETHING right. Anything. Is help on the way? As is our duty, we will monitor the progress and report to you each week. Just like we have been doing for forty two years now. Whew! Time passes, doesn’t it. Hint to the District and the Chiefs.

And The Lowly Chiefs
The NFL season is finally here. After a threatened strike, a boatload of free agents, and a new set of feet, the Chiefs will open at Arrowhead on Sunday. And you will see folks going to early morning church services, in order to witness the kickoff game to the 2011 season. And like the tornado that hit Joplin and the hurricane Irene that racked the east coast, the Chiefs have a lot of damage to clean up. You know they released All Pro offensive lineman, Brian Waters. Spt - Monday Nite Football

Monday Nite Football

Chiefs And Christmas

 Ring-a-ling, ring-a-ling. . .it’s football time again in the city.

 And our Kansas City Chiefs, full of vicissitudes, are back; and this time, it is crystal clear that the locals will still be struggling, come Christmas time.  In fact, some of us believe the Chiefs will be completely eliminated around Thanksgiving.    Let’s look a little closer.

 First, our Chiefs will have to play both Super Bowl teams. . . Chicago and Indianapolis.  That’s two down. 

 Then, we have to play San Diego twice. Remember, this team had a 14-2 record, the best in the NFL.  That’s two more losses.

 And we usually split with topsy-turvy Denver.  That makes

five losses, right off the bat. 

 Not to speak about Cincinnati,

Tennessee, and Minnesota.  Don’t forget about Oakland, who will be tougher just because they finally got a quarterback.  Essentially, the Chiefs can do no better than 8-8, this year. 

 Do I sound like Ike, Booker, Carl and Ollie?

 No, these are just the funky facts. The Chiefs are truly in trouble, face it. Now, this is not to say the Chiefs are entirely worthless.  For they have acquired some key gifts. . . Edwards and Bowe.  And there are some “lights” still glowing from last year. There is the perennial, Eddie Kenniston and league’s best running back, Larry Johnson. 

 On defense, there’s Tamba Hali and Derrick Johnson and even Jared Allen is all “lit up”. While none of these will set atop the Christmas tree, they were nonetheless promising, last year. Unfortunately, these are all ornaments; but there is no tree to put them on. So what am I saying?

 Santa or somebody needs to send us a quarterback and real quick. Herm is truly up-a-creek with both Brodie and Huard. Neither is of NFL quality and cannot help us win another playoff spot.  No way, these guys are going to make it, especially with the schedule I just mentioned.

 Now, Dr. Allen, Lloyd, and Cleaver are pretty loyal Chiefs fans.  And certainly they are to be congratulated for “hanging in there”. . . both in good times and bad.  But, for me, I’m headed straight to the Salvation Army and start the bell-ringing, next week. And I am encouraging each of you to attend church and begin your  prayers early.

 For it sure looks like a “lonesome Christmas”, coming up for the Chiefs.

 In a bad way, the Chiefs will be home for Christmas and in January, too.  Ring-a-ling.  Ring-a-ling.

Monday Nite Footballers

 Even Ike (Gardner) and that (Paul) Booker did not believe the Chiefs would lose 12 games.

 Those “two” plus Ed West and Carl Clark thought the Chiefs would break even at 8-8.

 Then, Lloyd Greenfield and even Congressman (Bubba) Cleaver joined the Haters, and began to predict their irreversible demise, especially after losing to lowly Oakland. And just think, they finally listened to the Monday Niters and got rid of (Mike) Solari, the offensive, offensive coordinator.

 And to remove all vestiges of a winning, (Dick) Vermeil era, they erased (James) Saxon and (Charlie) Joiner as assistants.

 Now, ol’ Herm (Edwards) and (Carl) Peterson will have their own draft and their own coaches. In plain English, they slickly blamed the disastrous 4-12 season on the assistant coaches, especially those that worked for the “town crier,” Vermeil.

 So, that means ol’ Herm and Emperor Carl will be in total charge of everything, alone and uninfluenced. So, we, as fans, can now hold them fully responsible for all that happens or doesn’t happen in 2008. Reluctantly, let’s give this ineffective duo another chance.

 Now, we all start out as fools and become wise through experience. If that African proverb is true, both Carl and Herm ought to share the King Solomon Wisdom award next year. Maybe, they can make Dr. Allen’s 11-5 prediction more likely.

 All jokes aside, 2007 is all over for Kansas City and now we must all throw our support to the San Diego Chargers and the Indianapolis Colts. That’s because the New England Patriots are about to go all-the-way.

 See ya on Super Bowl Friday.

frames.text: Allen, Charles (8)&hTab;&hTab;(16-0)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;Super Bowl Booker, Paul (7)&hTab;&hTab; (15-1)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab; Super Bowl Clark, Carl (8)&hTab;&hTab;(15-1)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;Super Bowl Cleaver, Bubba (8)&hTab;&hTab;(14-2)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;AFC Championship Gardner, Ike (6)&hTab;&hTab;(13-3)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;Division Playoffs Greenfield, Lloyd (8)&hTab;&hTab;(14-2)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;AFC Championship Hubbard, Ollie (8)&hTab;&hTab;(14-2)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;Super Bowl Nunnelly, Jim (8)&hTab;&hTab;(13-3)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;AFC Championship West, Ed (7)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;(14-2)&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;&hTab;Super Bowl The “Apostle” Paul Booker is the most liked guy among the Monday Niters.  He is low-key, dedicated and always avoids useless confrontations.  Quietly going about his life.  In fact, after leaving the Air Force, many years ago, he quietly enrolled at Lincoln University.  Not having any financial help, Booker had to clean up the state office buildings, at night, just to be able to go to school in the day.  Nobody knew his financial status.  As he began to make friends, there at Lincoln, he never imagined that those friends would become lifelong…..like Stewart Watson , Ollie Hubbard, Walt Livingston, and Charles Allen.  And, quietly, he carried those friendships forward, as he became an educator in the Kansas City School District and as an evening staff worker at the Niles Home for Children.  If Booker has an outspoken interest, it would be the plight of troubled youth.   As home-school coordinator under Ike Gardner, it was not uncommon for him to tirelessly search for services for the young people, assigned to him. In fact, a young man approached Booker one night, at a social gathering and thanked Booker for keeping him out of prison.  Now, that is Booker…at his best, helping youngsters who could go either way. Moreover,      Booker’s interest in football springs from his untiring interest in troubled youth.  He knows that many of the Chiefs have come from broken homes and with someone helping them, they have achieved in athletics.  Booker is always quietly, trying to help some youngster avoid being in trouble. Even though Booker is quiet, he is well-known around town.  In fact, a recent Mayor appointed Booker and another Monday Niter, to inspect metropolitan area night clubs, on Friday evenings. On a serious note, Booker is a well-liked, respected, quiet type of guy, everywhere he goes.

Niters.  He is low-key, dedicated and always avoids useless
confrontations.  Quietly going about his life.  In fact, after leaving
the Air Force, many years ago, he quietly enrolled at Lincoln
University.  Not having any financial help, Booker had to clean up the
state office buildings, at night, just to be able to go to school in the
day.  Nobody knew his financial status.  As he began to make friends,
there at Lincoln, he never imagined that those friends would become
lifelong…..like Stewart Watson , Ollie Hubbard, Walt Livingston, and
Charles Allen.  And, quietly, he carried those friendships forward, as
he became an educator in the Kansas City School District and as an
evening staff worker at the Niles Home for Children.  If Booker has an
outspoken interest, it would be the plight of troubled youth.   As
home-school coordinator under Ike Gardner, it was not uncommon for him
to tirelessly search for services for the young people, assigned to him.
In fact, a young man approached Booker one night, at a social gathering
and thanked Booker for keeping him out of prison.  Now, that is
Booker…at his best, helping youngsters who could go either way.
Moreover,      Booker’s interest in football springs from his untiring
interest in troubled youth.  He knows that many of the Chiefs have come
from broken homes and with someone helping them, they have achieved in
athletics.  Booker is always quietly, trying to help some youngster
avoid being in trouble. Even though Booker is quiet, he is well-known
around town.  In fact, a recent Mayor appointed Booker and another
Monday Niter, to inspect metropolitan area night clubs, on Friday
evenings. On a serious note, Booker is a well-liked, respected, quiet
type of guy, everywhere he goes.

frames.text: Chiefs Have  Taken  Us  Too Far, Too Fast, With  Too  Little Listening to the Chiefs' front office might lead you to believe that the Chiefs are going to the Super Bowl.  Wait a minute.  Grant you, the Chiefs are in first place in the Western Division of the American Conference.  And yes, they have more wins than losses (4-3).  And for you anti-Larry Johnson fans, the venerable Priest Holmes is back (at least for now).  And on an even brighter note, Dwayne Bowe is making the Chiefs look good on their first-round draft choice.  But, let's get real here. My advice to the Chiefs is "Don't take us too far, too fast, with too little". We are not even half-way through the season and we are shouting, as if the Chiefs have already achieved something.  Think about it. In November, the Chiefs still must face Green Bay and Denver at home and the undefeated Colts in Indianapolis.  Duh!  Now, the shouting should tone down a little.  And after our discussion last Monday night, there are great differences among us, as to how the Chiefs will fare, between now and Thanksgiving. Head Hater Ike Gardner and "that" Booker thinks the Chiefs will lose all three of those games.  That means that by the time we light up the Plaza, the Chiefs would have slipped to 4-6.  But Carl Clark is not going that far.  He thinks that the Chiefs will beat Denver and lose to Green Bay and the Colts. And just to give balance to the discussion, Ed West and Lloyd Greenfield think the Chiefs will beat both Green Bay and Denver and lose only to the Colts.  They think the Chiefs will be 6-4 by the time we all sit down to Thanksgiving dinner.  Now, the question is "who's right". Are the Chiefs taking us "too far, too fast, with too little".  As old-time fans, we've been down that yellow-brick road with the Chiefs before.  Win a few games and get us all excited and then, in the end, fall slowly to the bottom.  But this time, Lloyd and Ed are right on. The Chiefs will win at Arrowhead and lose in Indy. That being said, pass the mashed potatoes, please.

frames.text: Aaron Alexis, Mental Health Conference, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Aaron Alexis, Mental Health Conference, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Just like always, our country is faced with another mental health dilemma, Someone kills up a lot a people and we turn our attention to the crime, and not the events leading up to the horror. Thank God, we are going to have a conference here in Kansas City that will address the entire issue of mental health and mental illness. Yes, this Saturday at the Downtown Marriott, everyday folks will have an opportunity to talk about this woefully overlooked and under-discussed field. In fact, about 50 people from the urban core of Kansas City are signed up to participate in the day-long conversation. It’s all about planning and for once, we will be at the table, before it happens. Now, what does this all have to do with the now-winning Chiefs. Well, mental health controls everything we do. . . everything we think. . . and everything we try to do. And the Chiefs have been in a deep depression, for a long, long time. And now it appears that they are pulling themsellves out of it. That’s just what we all have to do. Address squarely the problem we are facing. The Chiefs went out and got a quarterback, some offensive linemen and a new coach. . . to address the losing streak and loss of fans. And they are gaining the fans back, with their early efforts in the season. Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Jim Nunnelly, and Ed West predicted that the Chiefs would win against Philadelphia. Of course, that cantankerous Ike Gardner and that garrulous Carl Clark thought the Chiefs have not changed, from last season. But face it, the depression is lifting. The Chiefs are talking and looking better these days. They are working hard at addressing the things that hurt them. Just like we as individuals should do. As we must do from time to time, we must remove cewrtain people from our lives. . .so that we can do better. In fact, the Chiefs are a lesson in regaining their mental health. So, Dr. Allen will be going to the conference on Saturday to talk about Alzheimer’s season. Jim Nunnelly will be addressing the stigma, associated with people who are struggling mentally. And Andrea Buford will be facilitating discussion tables, down at the Marriott. It will all be part of a historical time where we in the urban community, will be talking about the future and not arguing about the past. Maybe the first topic of discussion will be. . . how did the Chiefs overcome their depression. The answer is simple and complex. It took a lot of time, patience, and a lot of support from people who used to love them. All of you are invited to the Marriott on Saturday. Come see how to deal with mental health issues. With you becoming the focal point. . . for your own mental health.

frames.text: Okay, the Chiefs won one game.   It just so happened on national television and it was raining and the team we beat just happened to have won the AFC West Division last year. And for the first time in years, the Chiefs were part of the highlight reels on ESPN, as a positive. But just as sure as Todd Haley is not going to smile, the jury is still out on the Chiefs, at least the offense.  Speaking of offense, did you see Matt Cassel grab the game ball, as if he had something to do with the victory over San Diego? Make no mistake. . . that game ball should have gone to the defense, or the punt returner or the kickoff returner or Jamal Charles.  Definitely not the quarterback.   As we look ahead to Sunday, let’s see what the Monday Niters think about the upcoming game against Cleveland, in Cleveland. DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Monday night’s win over the Chargers was NOT a fluke.  Though improvement is still needed, the Chiefs will overtake the Browns by 10 points. THE APOSTLE PAUL BOOKER: I’m not that confident about the Chiefs, at least not yet. The Chiefs have gotten us all excited before, only to let us down. It is my firm belief that the Chiefs cannot and won’t beat Cleveland. End of story. COOL CARL CLARK: Unlike Booker, Carl believes the Chiefs CAN beat the Browns, if for no other reason that any team can beat another team on any given Sunday.  The Chiefs played good defense but the Chiefs’ quarterback is lacking an awful lot. CONGRESSMAN EMANUEL CLEAVER: From this point forward, the Chiefs will be measured by speed.  They got lots of speed, on the line, in the backfield, on special teams.  With that abundance of speed, they can and will beat Cleveland. CANTANKEROUS IKE GARDNER: The only place Ike is nice to people is out at a restaurant on 63rd.  There he is treated like royalty and he eats it up. But, his distrusting dislike for the Chiefs  While everyone else is raving about the Chiefs’ defense, Ike says the “the defense let us down”. Thus, Cleveland will beat our Chiefs on Sunday, according to Ike. LOYAL LLOYD GREENFIELD: He agrees that the win over San Diego was a fluke. But, he was glad to see the Chiefs win something. And for the record, he is backing the Chiefs this Sunday against the Browns.  Can we trust your judgement, Lloyd? OLLIE “KNOWS EVERYTHING” HUBBARD: Ollie is happy with the Chiefs.  You know he is part of the Ike and Booker thing that goes against the Chiefs.  But this time, Ollie joins up with the believers and picks Kansas City over Cleveland. JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY: Matt Cassel ain’t worth $60 million, y’all.  In fact, we would have killed San Diego with Brodie Croyle at quarterback.  He is drinking from wells that he didn’t dig.  But look for local writers and broadcasters to continue to make hi m an “unhung hero”. The only thing that didn’t work for the Chiefs was the offense. And guess who was the quarterback.  Get rid of him and the Chiefs will soar.  But, special teams are enough to beat Cleveland on Sunday. EASY ED WEST: Joining the believers is Ed West.  He flip-flops back and forth sometimes. But, this time, Ed is onto something. He thinks the Chiefs are young, hungry and motivated on both offense and defense.  Thus, his vote goes to the Chiefs to outclass Crennel’s old team, the Browns. ERIC “ERICA’S DAD” WESSON: There is an ole’ sayin’ “Even a hobo gets lucky and gets a steak every now and then if he hangs out in the right places.” That was what I was thinking in the Chiefs Monday victory, but it will be short lived.  The bottom line is the Chiefs lack the offensive players to be a household name. They won’t be able to score enough to beat Cleveland. Season record 4-12. FINAL NOTE:  The haters (Booker and that Ike) are the only ones, not believing in the Chiefs.  The believers are strong in their belief and feel that prayer has worked well for the Chiefs.  It certainly was not the coaching or the quarterback.  So after leaving early church on Sunday, look for the Chiefs to be 2-0, by three o’clock.  Believe, y’all.

COOL CARL CLARK: Unlike Booker, Carl believes the Chiefs CAN beat the Browns, if for no other reason that any team can beat another team on any given Sunday.  The Chiefs played good defense but the Chiefs’ quarterback is lacking an awful lot.

CONGRESSMAN EMANUEL CLEAVER: From this point forward, the Chiefs will be measured by speed.  They got lots of speed, on the line, in the backfield, on special teams.  With that abundance of speed, they can and will beat Cleveland.

CANTANKEROUS IKE GARDNER: The only place Ike is nice to people is out at a restaurant on 63rd.  There he is treated like royalty and he eats it up. But, his distrusting dislike for the Chiefs  While everyone else is raving about the Chiefs’ defense, Ike says the “the defense let us down”. Thus, Cleveland will beat our Chiefs on Sunday, according to Ike.

LOYAL LLOYD GREENFIELD: He agrees that the win over San Diego was a fluke. But, he was glad to see the Chiefs win something. And for the record, he is backing the Chiefs this Sunday against the Browns.  Can we trust your judgement, Lloyd?

The bottom line is the Chiefs lack the offensive players to be a household name. They won’t be able to score enough to beat Cleveland. Season record 4-12.

It certainly was not the coaching or the quarterback.  So after leaving early church on Sunday, look for the Chiefs to be 2-0, by three o’clock.  Believe, y’all.
