frames.text: By Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly Well, we all know that the Chiefs are still losing.  But, so is Oakland, the Chiefs’ next Arrowhead opponent.  And, we all know about the 40 year rivalry between the two teams.  And we also know that, at one time, these AFC stalwarts were competitive and even Super Bowl entrants.  But, like a lot of things, each of these two historical giants have fallen on “hard times”.  Neither is expected to do much at all, in 2008.  Like last year and the year before that.  In fact, these conference siblings are in a shaky state of re-building i.e. they will lose every game they play. Thus, the game out at Arrowhead  will be “a battle of the behinders”.  To mark such a sad occasion, I have changed the names of the teams, to reflect how even they are. . . in their likelihood to lose. From now on, these  two teams are called the Kansas City Raiders and the Oakland Chiefs.  That’s because they are both losers and they will continue doing “hard times of 2008”.   Enough said.  Allow me tell you a little about each one of the Monday Nite Footballers Group. . . one by one. . . with their predictions for Sunday. DR. CHARLES ALLEN (Kansas City) -- A dentist by profession. . . known for his painless procedures and his professional office staff. . a Kappa by fraternity.... an extraordinary grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by touchdown because the Chiefs will play better at home. PAUL BOOKER..(Oakland). . . retired educator...was a specialist in assisting needy students...hails from the Bootheel. . . watches ESPN everyday...good with figures...self-appointed liquor inspector...fantastic grandfather. . . believes Oakland will win by 10 because of the pitiful Chiefs’ pitiful offensive line. CARL CLARK (Kansas City). . . retired journeyman at Colgate...car enthusiast. world traveler...socially aware and respected. . . effective grandfather....daily visitor to 69th and Prospect. . . believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown, even though neither team is worthy of winning. BUBBA CLEAVER.(Kansas City). . . nationally-acclaimed elected official and minister. . . former Mayor and now United States Congressman. . .studious and thoughtful to a fault.. . . can remember thousands of people and their exact conversations. . . a proud grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by 10 because the Oakland Raiders don’t  “raid” any more. IKE GARDNER..(Oakland). . . fearless pragmatist. . . attends St. James and sits near the back on the aisle. . .a steadfast grandfather. . . cantankerous as hell. . . has seats on the 50 yard line at Arrowhead. . . was a key player in the early days of desegregation of schools. . .believes Kansas City by 3 because there is no chance for Oakland to win.  LLOYD GREENFIELD (Kansas City). . . a retired firefighter  turned real estate enthusiast. . . owns hundreds of model cars...has a motorcycle. . . has starred in many theatrical events. . . clear-headed and respected. . . stays in contact with his old high school class..believes the Chiefs will win by 3 but it will be on a “wing and a prayer”. OLLIE HUBBARD (Oakland). . . Loves and is married to Lincoln university. . . been known to lie about everything. . . knows everybody in Kansas City...formerly a vice principal, now retired....loves to prepare food for his friends so that he can eat the most.....a remarkable grandfather....thinks the Kansas City-Oakland game will be a toss-up but Chiefs could win by 14. JIM NUNNELLY..(Kansas City). . .has consulted with over 200 organizations nationwide....instrumental in building anddeveloping the Rodgers Health Center. . . .a relentless advocate for teenagers. . . a complete grandfather.......works at Jackson County. . . believes the Chiefs and the Raiders are the two worst teams in the NFL but come Sunday, the Chiefs will deploy a “Midwest Coast Defense” and win by 3. ED WEST....(Kansas City). . . a gadgetician. . . can construct or repair any computer...has a huge big screen tv. . .a substitute teacher in Raytown....was All-America at Pittsburg State. . .devout member of St. James. . . an encouraging grandfather...believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown because he “just a Raider-hater”

frames.text: You all remember Flip Wilson. He had his own television show, way back in the sixties. In fact, he was one of the first African American comedians to have a major white following. Most people will remember him as “Geraldine”, a cross-dressed character he created for the show. Everyone like ol’ Flip and he sure did a lot to reduce racial tensions, nationwide. Everyone waited for and watched Flip Wilson do his thing on Sunday evenings. Speaking of doing things, the Chiefs failed to win, out at Arrowhead this last Sunday. But don’t fret too much because they will be still be playing after they play Sunday against the Chargers.. That simply means they have played well enough and won enough games to “qualify” for the Super Bowl chase.  However, two things. They have to win to stay in the mix. And secondly, they have to play on the road. Now, remember when the Chiefs won the Super Bowl after the 1969 season, they were in the same position. They were a wild card entry, which means they can pursue the Super Bowl….but they have to play on the road. If you want to know more about the only Super Bowl the Chiefs have played in, just ask Ike Gardner. He is still mad because the Chiefs have never regained the respect they once had, when they won the “big game” against the Joe Kapp and the Minnesota Vikings. Speaking of Ike and his cantankerous ways, I owe him somewhat of an apology. You will remember last week, I talked about how Ike had consistently beat up on the Chiefs. In spite of them winning eleven games this year, he still insists they are a mediocre team at best. Truthfully, they are much more than they were last year. But last Sunday against Indianapolis , they stunk. I mean less than mediocre. After the first series touchdown, the Chiefs went downhill, the rest of the game. Thatcaused national commentators to talk badly about the Chiefs, as well. They say that the Chiefs can’t win against teams with winning tradition and records. That sounds like what Ike has been saying. Really, I don’t mind what Ike says. I just don’t like the way he says it. There’s no love or loyalty in his cantankerous comments. He sounds so disloyal. Unlike other Monday Niters like Dr. Allen, Paul Booker, Carl Clark, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Ollie Hubbard and Ed West, Ike just blatantly “tells it like it is”. And readers everywhere just are appalled at his non-support of the home team. But another old saying may apply. “It is what it is”. The Chiefs are shaky some days. But some days, they show great promise, especially among players like Derrick Johnson and Jamaal Charles and even Tamba Hali. Another old saying is that “you can’t make a silk purse out of a pig’s ear”. That means you have to accept what the Chiefs are and they are a good team…but not a great team like New England or Denver or New Orleans or even Seattle. Ike would say the Chiefs will not make it through the first round in the playoffs. But they made it this far and they will be trying to advance. And they will be on tv, when most teams will be watching. Getting back to tv, we started out talking about Flip Wilson having his own tv show, way back when. And like all of our favorite shows, something is said that sticks with us all of our life. And it just may well wrap up this conversation about the Chiefs. Old Flip used to say somewhere during every telecast. What You See Is What You Get” And that my friends describes our Kansas City Chiefs. So Ike needs to call on Flip to help him state his disdain, more appropriately.

frames.text: Every time, we go to Ed West’s house, the sparks fly.   First on our list was to compliment the Chiefs on a good effort.   Enough said. Instead, we talked about who should be fired in the Chiefs’ front office.   But, then we began to predict if Barack Obama would actual win the highest elective office in our nation.  Here’s a summary of the discussions from some of the most opinionated, talkative, and knowledgeable guys in Kansas City. DR. CHARLES ALLEN: He thinks the whole coaching squad ought to be sacked, especially Günther Cunningham and Carl Peterson, the Chiefs’ General Manager and President.. . .Charles is “guardedly optimistic” about Obama’s chances to become President of the United States. . . still thinks the Chiefs will win at Arrowhead. . . Chiefs by 3 PAUL BOOKER:   Paul thinks the Hunts ought to “sweep clean” the whole staff, management and coaches.  . . .Paul has a “gut” feeling about Obama’s chances to become President. . .He doesn’t feel the Chiefs will have a chance on Sunday. . .Tampa Bay by 21. CARL CLARK: He, too, thinks Günther is the problem with the Chiefs and must be the first to go. . .Unlike Booker, Carl thinks Obama will win but by a very small margin. . . he has no doubts as to who will win Sunday. . . Tampa Bay by 14. BUBBA CLEAVER: Unlike the rest of us, feels that the problem is not only in the coaching ranks. . . he thinks it is Larry Johnson who is the disruptive force on the Chiefs. . . In the same line of reasoning, Cleaver believes that Obama will win by a small margin. . . Believes Warren Dunn will do what he has “done” to other teams. . . run them raggedy..Tampa Bay by 10. IKE GARDNER:  Ike was rather nice on Monday night, he only called Carl Clark out of his name only once. . . He hopes Obama will win but was quick to remind everyone that elections can be stolen and referred us back to the Gore-Bush crap in Florida. . . He thinks the Buccaneers will find their pot of gold at Arrowhead Sunday. . . Tampa Bay by 21. LLOYD GREENFIELD: Forcefully, Lloyd thinks Carl Peterson should go today. . . then, Günther Cunningham. . . He thinks the “undecided” will favor McCain but Obama will emerge as winner. . .he thinks the Chiefs are still “trick or treating”. . . Tampa Bay by 14. OLLIE HUBBARD:  Ollie feels that Carl Peterson and Herman Edwards should be given a one-way ticket. . . Obama will win “hands down” unless the cheaters emerge. . .he is so disappointed that he has to go to against the Chiefs. . . Tampa Bay by 40 JIM NUNNELLY:   He feels that Herm Edwards must set the tone for winning and he has not done that. . . No excuse, Herm must go.. . . He feels that it will be a long night because of the long voting lines and there will be procedural issues for several days. . . but in the end, Obama will be our next President of the United States. . . He has not given up on the Chiefs...Chiefs by 6. ED WEST:   No doubt about it, Ed thinks Carl Peterson is and always has been the Chiefs’ problem. . . Ed thinks Obama will get sufficient electoral votes to win. . . thinks Tampa Bay will jump on the Chiefs’ shipwreck. . .Tampa Bay by 20

frames.text: The Chiefs suck.   End of conversation.   Fortunately, the Monday Niters talk about more than the vicissitudes of this so-called professional football team. Out at Dr. Allen’s house, amid the Greek-influenced, romaine-based salad and another Greek concoction, man we talked about old remedies, used by our folks in the thirties and forties.  And we focused our attention on some special senior citizens, those that are permanently imprinted in our memories.  Congressman Cleaver called from Washington to share some news about the over-demanded/under-supplied inaugural tickets. So, instead of beating some “dead Chiefs”, let’s look in on a not-so-typical Monday Niter word-fest. DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Charles is sending Mrs. Mila Banks a special, belated Birthday wish.  She believes the Chiefs will eventually develop into a fine team.  That’s just like Charles, going out and recruiting people who still think the Chiefs can win. Mila says that the Monday Niters are “. . .men of little faith”.  Right you are! But Charles isn’t. . . CHIEFS BY; 3 PAUL BOOKER:  Booker is usually a nice guy, except when it comes to the Chiefs.  Then, he turns into this “killer monster”, thinking that the Chiefs have no offense at all.  He did smile when he acknowledged the wisdom and faith of his 84-year-old sister from Hayti, Missouri.  This lady bore and reared thirteen children, in her lifetime.  Booker says his mom used the yellow of an egg to reduce the swelling, caused by Mumps.  Okkkkkkk! Anyway, BUFFALO BY 13 CARL CLARK: Carl claimed that his folks cured him of pneumonia by using skunk oil and honey.  That one doesn’t pass the smell test.  Carl mentioned seeing Mila Banks around town, especially at social events like Ivanhoe and Twin City functions.  “She always talks about the Chiefs”, said Carl smiling.  Smile or no smile. Smell or no smell.  The Chiefs will be stampeded Sunday. . .BUFFALO BY 14 BUBBA CLEAVER:  Cleaver is stuck in Washington, fighting for the bailout of the automakers.  He says he cannot vote any other way because 2,000 or more jobs will be lost here in Kansas City, if he doesn’t support the bailout.  Cleaver called the Monday Niters and told them he is being besieged with inaugural ticket requests.  He is planning a lottery to address the thousands of requests...In the meantime, he thinks the Chiefs still have not found a way to win. . . BUFFALO BY 14. IKE GARDNER:  Ike believes the Chiefs are going to get a steady diet of Buffalo chips, Sunday.  Ike has lost friends because of his no-patience position with the Chiefs.  But he did smile when he spoke of Mila Banks.  He remembers her as a great teacher at R.T. Coles.  Ike even congratulated Mila for being such a fearless disciplinarian, something sorely needed in today’s schools. During the discussion about home remedies, Ike came up with something called “juniper tar and sugar” for colds.  Will this work for the Chiefs?  Apparently not. . .  BUFFALO BY 13 LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Lloyd said there was something called “666” for colds.  Is this some kind of devil reference?  And Lloyd chimed in about Mila Banks being at a recent Ivanhoe party.  Lloyd reminded Mila that he was one of her late husband’s “jelly beans” (a term used frequently for students by Isaiah Banks).  Speaking of jelly beans, Lloyd thinks that the Chiefs can’t even beat a piece of candy.  BUFFALO BY 10 OLLIE HUBBARD  Ollie talks with Mila Banks often, to check on her.  Ollie said Mila and her friends went down to visit Carl Connor in Columbia recently.  Growing up on 27th and Olive, Ollie says his mother gave him turpentine and sugar for colds.  If the cold got real bad, she would apply “goose grease” all over his huge body. But, nothing can help these Chiefs with a win.  Look for number 10 loss, Sunday. . . BUFFALO BY 20 JIM NUNNELLY:  He brought up  Carl Connor, who now resides in Columbia, Mo., near his nephew, Charles Allen.   Connor reads this column religiously, even though he is at least ninety five.  He is alert and like Mila, taught here in the Kansas City, Mo., School District for years.  Carl is and has always been a Missouri Tiger sports fan.  That’s good news because the Chiefs sure ain’t doing much. In Columbia, the old folks thought Vick’s saffe would cure colds, pneumonia, hangovers. . .everything.  But, it can’t help the Chiefs BUFFALO BY 30 ED WEST:  Ed is from rural Kansas and like all rural families, they relied on certain remedies for survival.  His family consumed a lot of iron supplement, called 3-S Tonic.  It must have helped because Ed is a picture of health and still uses “Three S” everyday.  It seems that the Chiefs are taking something these days for they are definitely improving.  But, according to Ed, not enough.  BUFFALO BY 10.

frames.text: For the most part, we again ignored the awful plight of the Kansas City Chiefs, this past Monday.  We were entertained at Ike’s house, out in Raytown.  Ike claims he fixed the red beans and rice, laced with gumbo-like polish sausages and topped with onions.  His family came to his rescue, with Lura, Shelley and Roosevelt providing various levels of hospitality.  And the Chiefs, on a bye week, did not provide much conversational opportunities.  Thus, the conversation drifted into lots of words about Lincoln University’s Homecoming weekend. Being alumni, several of our members attended the long-weekend and were greeted with the Temptations and a great half-time show, at the football game.  Of particular note was the maturing Lincoln University Marching Band.  Ollie Gates, favorite of old’ L.U., made his annual trek to Jefferson City, parked his motor-home on the football field, and provided Lincoln’s President with his annual donation. But, Lincoln has changed dramatically, since the days of segregation.  In fact, Lincoln is quite diverse, with many drive-in, day students having enrolled since the early seventies.  That’s why it is referred to as an “historically black college and university”. So while the Chiefs will get slaughtered at Arrowhead Sunday, much of the conversation, for us, concentrated on an important topic, like Lincoln University. Unlike the Chiefs, Lincoln beat Xavier 56-7. DR. CHARLES ALLEN  Proud alumni of Lincoln...attended the homecoming ceremonies last week and immediately noticed a major difference, compared to the sixties...there were curfews then, especially for girls...there were no co-ed dorms.. this year, the Homecoming queen, a beautiful black lady, was escorted by a Caucasian guy.....and Charles clearly missed the “foot”, a collection of joints at the bottom of the famous hills...he missed Miss Leona’s famous chili-skillet-stew...she made sure that no Lincoln student ever went hungry....no coming back y’all...but Charles believes that the Chiefs are saying that “a setback is a set-up for a come-back” and predicts CHIEFS BY 7 PAUL BOOKER  Also an alumni from the Bootheel...also misses Miss Leona’s cooking that combined everything into a single dish....Booker ate there twice a day because he hated the campus food...looks forward to meeting all of his old friends at Edna Brannock’s mother’s house each year...liked the Temptations. but coming back from Jefferson City, thought about the Chiefs and just knew that the Titans will Tennessee-waltz the Chiefs...TENNESSEE BY 13. CARL CLARK  Carl was rather quiet, this past Monday...in fact, he fell into a deep sleep a couple of times....usually talkative but rather subdued....he enjoyed attending Lincoln’s homecoming during his high school days...he didn’t go back after a girl threw some chitterlings on Apple Jack...he hasn’t been back since. someone must have thrown some chitlins on the Chiefs....Carl predicts TENNESSEE BY 14. IKE GARDNER  Ike’s affiliation with Lincoln arose because he was refused admission to Missouri University and they, then, suggested he enrolled at Lincoln, instead....noted that most black colleges, including Howard where he attended, had curfews based on the day of the week, allowing later times as the week progressed...did not ever attend Lincoln but has been a staunch supporter of HBCU’s...turning to the Chiefs, Ike is not impressed with Chiefs at all...thinks they can’t stop rolling downhill...TENNESSEE BY 25. LLOYD GREENFIELD  His cousin, Charlene Boswell attended Lincoln university....she was instrumental in organizing the Metropolitan Spiritual church...Lloyd was a sprinter at Lincoln High School way back in the early fifties....is producing a cd, featuring singers Jackie Mackrel and Geneva Price....keeps asking the question...have you ever seen a Tennessean walk....well, TENNESSEE BY 14. OLLIE HUBBARD  Graduated from Lincoln University in 1966....a major contributor to Lincoln....impressed with the growth of Lincoln over the years...attended “every” homecoming between 1967 and 2005, stopping because of a leg problems...salutes all the Kansas Citians who have attended Lincoln, including Donna Stewart, Ollie Gates, Georgia Buchanan, Bob Wheeler, and Gurnie Gunther...while he still plans to support Lincoln university, he has given up on the Chiefs entirely...TENNESSEE BY 30. JIM NUNNELLY  He chose to enroll at Missouri University, even though he had a full scholarship to Lincoln....attended several homecomings...as a high school student, won the Armistead Pride Journalism award three years in a row...lived in Columbia and knew many Lincoln alumni, including Erma Monroe, Juanita Dixon, Mary Patton, Joanne Herndon, Emma Turner, George Brooks, Montell Washington....lot of years have left by but not his faith in the Chiefs...CHIEFS BY 3 ED WEST  Believes the Chiefs’ losing streak is about to take off...was a track and football athlete at Pittsburg State...competed in the long jump against Herman Gant...who was a miler at Lincoln.....Gant is still in great shape and walked every day from the Capitol hotel to the Lincoln campus during Lincoln’s Homecoming...like the rest of us, Ed is just plain tired of the Chiefs....TENNESSEE BY 30. ROOSEVELT SCULARK  Ike’s son-in-law....alumni of Jackson State and Howard, both hbcu’s...interacted with the Monday Niters throughout the evening...clean-cut and credible...believes the Chiefs’ secondary cannot stop anything or anybody...TENNESSEE BY 24...

frames.text: The winning ways of the Chiefs are gone forever....like home-made pies, real mashed potatoes, pan-fried chicken, John Agnos pig-ear sandwiches, the Birdland, 20-mens Club, Frank’s Place etc.  While we may be melancholy about them, they are not coming back.  Our grandchildren will just have to take our word for it. DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Possesses a surreal optimism about the Chiefs. . ..his grandson Robert is a free safety at Grandview Middle...Robert has been with Charles and Beverly since he was 14 months old.believes Kansas City will beat Denver by 14. (Wake up Dr. Allen, have you been to the 6902?) PAUL BOOKER:  Probably the least controversial of all the Monday Nite Footballers...pleasant style. . . serves a buffet of fine choices...brags all the time about his granddaughter Ashley, who is starting point guard at Penn Valley. . .thinks Denver will show no mercy, Sunday...Denver by 14. CARL CLARK:  Has the distinction of having both his grandchildren named in his honor, Carl III and Carlynn. . . owns a slick Corvette. . . just elected chairman of the 6902 Board of Directors. . . believes the Chiefs will not win another game...Denver by14. BUBBA CLEAVER:  will present at the national Congressional Black Caucus on foreclosures. . . talks often to his grandchildren by phone. . . they don’t care about his community standing. . . has over a thousand eight-track tapes. . . nicknamed the stadium Arrowhead United Methodist Church. . . thinks the Chiefs are a cinch to lose again.  Bubba will leave on Sunday to visit the Missouri National Guard troops in Kosovo, Yugoslavia. Denver by 14 IKE GARDNER:  Once put a “no visitors” sign on his hospital-room door...has the personality of an injured wolverine. . . once volunteered for his teacher-daughter Tia. . . takes his nine-year-old grandson Isaiah to 35 Chiefs football games. . . the only dog he ever owned ran away, seeking asylum at Wayside Waifs. . . will have a BIG Birthday on September 26. . . believes the Chiefs are no opposition for Denver...Broncos by 35. LLOYD GREENFIELD: Is responsible for assuring that all Monday Niters receive an annual dose of culture by arranging to attend a play in the area. . . is new in the “grandfather” role for his seven-month-old granddaughter, Geneva. . . wants to provide her with a good foundation because he never had one. . . is considering wearing a toupee. . . bald or not, believes Chiefs have too many internal problems to win. . . Denver by 14 1/2. OLLIE HUBBARD:  Is one of the best fish-cooks in the Kansas City area. . .has cooked many a fish and made a lot of chili raising funds for Lincoln University . . . rescued his now wife from one of the largest cities in Missouri, Macon. . . has more out of town visitors than the entire hotel industry. . . loves to go to Mount Pleasant, Texas. . . believes the Broncos will kill the Chiefs. Denver by 35. JIM NUNNELLY:  All four of his grandchildren are named in his honor....grandson Chris now attending Missouri Western at St. Joseph. . .hails from Columbia, Missouri. . .featured in Ebony magazine in 1975. . .can be seen at Gates, Niecies, Peachtree, M and M Bakery all the time. . . wife, Janice never cooks. . . will one day write a book about these Monday Nite Footballers. . .moans for the “good ol’ days”. . .they are never coming back. . .no Dante Hall, no victory...Denver by 28. ED WEST: Has two adolescent granddaughters in California. . .son Damon was the music producer for “Dreamgirls”. . . had a strong influence on his son’s career by enrolling him in Christian School. . ..can fix anything electronic. . . was the audio engineer at St. James. . . wife, Celeste is an advocate for alternative school students. . . believes the defense will be Cutlerized. Denver by 20.

frames.text: No one knows what these Chiefs are going to do this season.  Everyone is so righteously caught up in the training camp move to St. Joseph, as if where a team practices wins football games.  Nah, it ain’t happening.  It still counts what happens on the field, starting the second week in September.  But, we Monday Niters are admittedly getting swooped up by the hype.   As the guys gather every Friday at a local club, the Chiefs and the 2010 season dominates the discussion.  Of course, the oldies but goodies music helps them reminisce about the good old days, when the Chiefs really were Chiefs. . . not Chefs.  But here is some of the pre-season chatter going on at 69th and Prospect. TRIVIA QUESTION FOR THE WEEK: What teams played in the last Super Bowl? 1) Ed West is steadily teaching his fellow Monday Niters about technology.  Armed with a i-phone, Ed is able to respond quickly to any football question that needs a quick answer.  Where there once was arguments, now it is a simple...talk-into-the-phone and within a few seconds, there is a bona fide answer.  He also got Carl to buy one of those nifty phones.  And Ike even bought a laptop.  So did Nunnelly.  And Booker is actually going to Best Buy every week to look at one.  2)  All the talk this week is about the upcoming weekend Hall of Fame game. frames.text: Monday Niters Johnny Cash, Memorable Ministers And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Monday Niters
Johnny Cash, Memorable Ministers And The Chiefs

frames.text: About 50 years ago, Johnny Cash recorded a song, called, “A Boy Named Sue”.  Well, the Chiefs are going to face a “Man Called Suh”. He was last year’s  “Defensive Rookie Of The Year” in the NFL. His complete name is Ndamudong Suh (pronounced N dam u kong). This unusual name is African and it means “house of spears”. He is 6’4” tall and hails from Portland, Oregon. That where his Cameroon-born father and Jamaica-born mother resides. What does that have to do with the Chiefs? Well, the paper-thin, Chiefs’ offense will have to face Ndamukong Suh and the rest of the Detroit Lions on Sunday. It’s at noon and you can look for this man named “Suh” to be all over  and all in the Chiefs’ backfield, just throwing Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel and Once In A While Jamal Charles all over the place. Not bad for a boy named “Sue”. Well, we Monday Niters met over at Ike’s house and had some show-stopping cherry cobbler. Though he didn’t prepare the multi-faceted meal, he walked around kingly, like he was part of it. Truth is his wife, their daughter Shelly and her daughter Danielle prepared every dish and yet, Cantankerous Ike tried to take credit for such a culinary display. A minister would have concluded that he is richly blessed. Speaking of ministers, that was the main topic of our conversations. Here goes, along with our predictions. Dr. Charles Allen: He remembered Rev. John Williams at the St. Stephen Baptist church. But, he also praised Father Benedict Justice, one of the few black Catholic priests in Kansas City in the ‘40s and ‘50s. But reluctantly and against all religions, he believes in the locals. Chiefs by 3 The Apostle Paul Booker:  He praised the Reverend Henderson Bell, his home-church pastor. He considers his pastor as the most approachable minister in town. But Paul doesn’t believe in The Chiefs at all. Detroit by 14 Carl “Righteous Bro-ther” Clark: He was married at the Mason Memorial in Kansas 50 two years ago. But, he has always attended St. James, under Rev. Cleaver, the only minister he has ever known. And he doesn’t know the Chiefs anymore, either. Detroit by 14 Ike “One Mean PaPaw” Gardner: Ike is so spoiled by a group of waitresses at a popular restaurant that he sometimes forgets that he is not a priest of man of the cloth. But he does remember being forced to go to church at Ward’s Chapel, years ago.  Since then, he has bonded with Rev. Cleaver and now is an unforced member of St. James. Like him or not, he says no. Detroit by 20 Lloyd “Gentleman” Greenfield: Right off, Lloyd remembered Reverend Chapelle of the Second Baptist Church, as a minister who could related to young black males. Awesome man. But still sticking with the locals. Chiefs by 7 Congressman Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver II: Being a minister himself, Cleaver had several ministers on his praise list. . .Reverends A.L. Johnson, John Preciphs, Emanuel Newton, John Eason. Isaiah Henderson Sr. and many others. But he got carried away and also praised the Chiefs. Chiefs by 8 Jim “GrandDad” Nunnelly: He praised Rev. Earl Abel for his excellence as a pastor and a friend.  Also for mentoring and selecting the very capable Reverend Leonard Butler as his successor. A good pick for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7 Ed “Mentor Man” West: Besides being a computer guru, Ed spends his time, mentoring young males over at Raytown High school.  He is so good at it that he sometimes is referred to as a minister. Not so but his hero is Reverend Cleaver ever since he came here from Osawatomie,  Kas. No religion for the Chiefs. Detroit by 40 Ollie “Barbara Walters” Hubbard: Ollie knows everybody and everything. He reached way back to choose Reverend D.A. Holmes as his most memorable minister, a namesake for elderly homes and a school. But still believes the Chiefs will get a good education Sunday. Detroit by 40

About 50 years ago, Johnny Cash recorded a song, called, “A Boy Named Sue”.

Well, the Chiefs are going to face a “Man Called Suh”. He was last year’s “Defensive Rookie Of The Year” in the NFL. His complete name is Ndamudong Suh (pronounced N dam u kong). This unusual name is African and it means “house of spears”. He is 6’4” tall and hails from Portland, Oregon. That where his Cameroon-born father and Jamaica-born mother resides.

What does that have to do with the Chiefs? Well, the paper-thin, Chiefs’ offense will have to face Ndamukong Suh and the rest of the Detroit Lions on Sunday. It’s at noon and you can look for this man named “Suh” to be all over and all in the Chiefs’ backfield, just throwing Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel and Once In A While Jamal Charles all over the place.

Not bad for a boy named “Sue”.

Well, we Monday Niters met over at Ike’s house and had some show-stopping cherry cobbler. Though he didn’t prepare the multi-faceted meal, he walked around kingly, like he was part of it. Truth is his wife, their daughter Shelly and her daughter Danielle prepared every dish and yet, Cantankerous Ike tried to take credit for such a culinary display. A minister would have concluded that he is richly blessed. Speaking of ministers, that was the main topic of our conversations. Here goes, along with our predictions.

Dr. Charles Allen: He remembered Rev. John Williams at the St. Stephen Baptist church. But, he also praised Father Benedict Justice, one of the few black Catholic priests in Kansas City in the ‘40s and ‘50s. But reluctantly and against all religions, he believes in the locals. Chiefs by 3

The Apostle Paul Booker: He praised the Reverend Henderson Bell, his home-church pastor. He considers his pastor as the most approachable minister in town. But Paul doesn’t believe in The Chiefs at all. Detroit by 14

Carl “Righteous Bro-ther” Clark: He was married at the Mason Memorial in Kansas 50 two years ago. But, he has always attended St. James, under Rev. Cleaver, the only minister he has ever known. And he doesn’t know the Chiefs anymore, either. Detroit by 14

Ike “One Mean PaPaw” Gardner: Ike is so spoiled by a group of waitresses at a popular restaurant that he sometimes forgets that he is not a priest of man of the cloth. But he does remember being forced to go to church at Ward’s Chapel, years ago. Since then, he has bonded with Rev. Cleaver and now is an unforced member of St. James. Like him or not, he says no. Detroit by 20

Lloyd “Gentleman” Greenfield: Right off, Lloyd remembered Reverend Chapelle of the Second Baptist Church, as a minister who could related to young black males. Awesome man. But still sticking with the locals. Chiefs by 7

Congressman Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver II: Being a minister himself, Cleaver had several ministers on his praise list. . .Reverends A.L. Johnson, John Preciphs, Emanuel Newton, John Eason. Isaiah Henderson Sr. and many others. But he got carried away and also praised the Chiefs. Chiefs by 8

Jim “GrandDad” Nunnelly: He praised Rev. Earl Abel for his excellence as a pastor and a friend. Also for mentoring and selecting the very capable Reverend Leonard Butler as his successor. A good pick for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7

Ed “Mentor Man” West: Besides being a computer guru, Ed spends his time, mentoring young males over at Raytown High school. He is so good at it that he sometimes is referred to as a minister. Not so but his hero is Reverend Cleaver ever since he came here from Osawatomie, Kas. No religion for the Chiefs. Detroit by 40

Ollie “Barbara Walters” Hubbard: Ollie knows everybody and everything. He reached way back to choose Reverend D.A. Holmes as his most memorable minister, a namesake for elderly homes and a school. But still believes the Chiefs will get a good education Sunday. Detroit by 40

frames.text: Chiefs, Not At All Like Beyonce

paragraphs.text: Chiefs, Not At All Like Beyonce

frames.text: Beyonce in her new album says “I woke up like this”. That means she was not taught, nor did she acquire any of her great talents. Inferentially, she is saying that she was “born” with such entirety. Let’s see how that applies to the Chiefs, after their rather surprising win over Miami. But before that, let’s record what happened over to Paul Booker’s house recently. First, we talked about the upcoming community conversation about Health. Sponsored by the Healthcare Foundation, this big conversation will take place on October 11, down at the Sheraton Hotel in Crown Center. Everyone can come but you must register. More important, all of the Monday Niters will be there, expressing their views on behalf of the central city elderly. So, the guys just gave a sample of the things they will promote and say, during this high-tech conversation.  Dr. Charles Allen and Paul Booker want to see more health programs, addressing mental health and Alzheimer’s disease.  And Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield and Carl Clark expressed the critical need to address diabetes. They say that this diabetes thing is rampant and will speak collectively for those thousands of uncontrolled diabetics. And Ed West chimes in about the need for nursing home reform and the lack of adequate health insurance among our elderly brothers and sisters. In fact, the Monday Niters will be working with elderly organizations like the Palestine Senior Citizens Center to get their support. It is the goal to have fifty central city elderly persons at that conference. The business, at hand, is clear. Speaking of business, the guys started reminiscing again. Last week, it was about health care providers. This year, they switched to entrepreneurs of the past.  Here are some of the names that emerged from the early Kansas City days:. G.L. Blankenship (beauty products); George and Ollie Gates (barbq); Madame C. J. Walker (cosmetics); Fannie Meeks (funeral services); Sarah Rector (real estate); Everett O’Neal (security); Earl Pitts (tire company); Leon Arnold (real estate); Chuck Wimes (mortgage lending);  and Roy Walker (electrician). These brave men and women really set the tone for Kansas City’s rise to international fame and are the maverick heroes of our past.  Speaking of heroes, the Chiefs had several, last week in their win over Miami. Knile Davis ran wild, making us think that Jamaal Charles had better get well quick. And certainly, McKnight was a pleasant surprise, catching two touchdown passes. And the defense showed that there is some hope that they will jell, some day. But the real message is not at all like Beyonce’s. The Chiefs were not born,  like they played Saturday. It is and has been a struggle, every step of the way. Eleven starters hurt. A bunch of undrafted  no-names. A highly-paid but inconsistent quarterback. An ineffective offensive line. All of this adds up to a severe lack of “entirety”. Up till now, the Chiefs could and would not impress Beyonce, at all. Now, Denver and Seattle have that Beyonce-like- entirety, displaying “seasoned excellence”, on every down and every Sunday. The Chiefs only have to dream about this kind of play. So let’s not get too happy over last Sunday’s win. That’s because the New England Patriots  will be coming to town Monday, playing the Chiefs before a nationally televised audience. And they Patriots will be playing like Beyonce sings and dances, repeating to themselves often  that “they woke up like this”.  Like Mila Banks, we all hope the Chiefs will continue upward. But who knows about those Chiefs? They are quite “sometimey” and they can change in a New York minute. But, here’s what the guys think will happen at Arrowhead on Monday night: Dr. Charles Allen      Patriots are not what they used to be Chiefs by 10 Mila Banks                 Really hope this winning continues                Chiefs  by 10 Paul Booker              The Brady factor is real                                      Patriots by 14 Carl Clark                  KC’s offensive line is still limited                       Patriots by 14 Bubba Cleaver         By Tuesday morning, both teams are 2-2 Chiefs by 10 Ike Gardner             Little boys are not ready for the Big Boys       Patriots by 17 Lloyd Greenfield    On a wing and a prayer                                      Chiefs by 10 Ollie Hubbard         Like Donna Summers, K.C. will survive Chiefs by 7 Jim Nunnelly          Like Jay Z, the Chiefs find  the Holy Grail         Chiefs by 3 Ed West                  Offensive weapons return                                   Chiefs by 1

Chiefs, Not At All Like Beyonce
Beyonce in her new album says “I woke up like this”. That means she was not taught, nor did she acquire any of her great talents. Inferentially, she is saying that she was “born” with such entirety. Let’s see how that applies to the Chiefs, after their rather surprising win over Miami. But before that, let’s record what happened over to Paul Booker’s house recently.
First, we talked about the upcoming community conversation about Health. Sponsored by the Healthcare Foundation, this big conversation will take place on October 11, down at the Sheraton Hotel in Crown Center. Everyone can come but you must register. More important, all of the Monday Niters will be there, expressing their views on behalf of the central city elderly. So, the guys just gave a sample of the things they will promote and say, during this high-tech conversation.
Dr. Charles Allen and Paul Booker want to see more health programs, addressing mental health and Alzheimer’s disease.  And Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield and Carl Clark expressed the critical need to address diabetes. They say that this diabetes thing is rampant and will speak collectively for those thousands of uncontrolled diabetics. And Ed West chimes in about the need for nursing home reform and the lack of adequate health insurance among our elderly brothers and sisters. In fact, the Monday Niters will be working with elderly organizations like the Palestine Senior Citizens Center to get their support. It is the goal to have fifty central city elderly persons at that conference. The business, at hand, is clear.
Speaking of business, the guys started reminiscing again. Last week, it was about health care providers. This year, they switched to entrepreneurs of the past.
Here are some of the names that emerged from the early Kansas City days:. G.L. Blankenship (beauty products); George and Ollie Gates (barbq); Madame C. J. Walker (cosmetics); Fannie Meeks (funeral services); Sarah Rector (real estate); Everett O’Neal (security); Earl Pitts (tire company); Leon Arnold (real estate); Chuck Wimes (mortgage lending);  and Roy Walker (electrician). These brave men and women really set the tone for Kansas City’s rise to international fame and are the maverick heroes of our past.
Speaking of heroes, the Chiefs had several, last week in their win over Miami. Knile Davis ran wild, making us think that Jamaal Charles had better get well quick. And certainly, McKnight was a pleasant surprise, catching two touchdown passes. And the defense showed that there is some hope that they will jell, some day. But the real message is not at all like Beyonce’s. The Chiefs were not born,  like they played Saturday. It is and has been a struggle, every step of the way. Eleven starters hurt. A bunch of undrafted  no-names. A highly-paid but inconsistent quarterback. An ineffective offensive line. All of this adds up to a severe lack of “entirety”. frames.text: Apogee is a word, used in astronomy to describe the farther point out there in space. It was used in the novel, Fifty Shades Of Grey to describe the best feeling that can be derived from romantic encounter. Well, on Sunday, the apogee of football games will be played in New Orleans. This game will feature Baltimore Ravens and the San Francisco Forty Niners. San Francisco will probably win, mainly because of its stellar quarterback, Kaepernick. This kid is “on fire” and will silence the tirades and mental health outbreaks of Ray Lewis. Ray can stir up the crowd but this kid can move the ball down the field. In fact, over half of his passes go for twenty yards or more. His actions speak louder than Ray Lewis’ words. He is arguably the best quarterback in the league. Speaking of quarterbacks, why can’t the Chiefs buy, borrow or beg for a good quarterback? Other teams do this but Kansas City cannot get it done. That’s why the Chiefs are “left out” and left at home. You would think that a team with six Pro Bowlers can at least find one quarterback, among all these youngsters. And they are not promising that the quarterback position is not their highest draft priority. That attitude is just plain stupid and explains why the Chiefs haven’t been in a Superbowl, since 1970. So while San Francisco and Baltimore will be kicking it in the SuperDome, the Kansas City Chiefs will be looking wise and otherwise and missing the point. paragraphs.text: Nat ‘King’ Cole, The Christmas
Song, And The 10-3 Chiefs

frames.text: For those of you under 50, you probably missed a treat, not hearing all the songs ever recorded by Nat “King”Cole.   Every year about this time, that smooth, velvety voice makes its way into our ears, hearts, and mind. And for us over fifty, we recall that Ol’ King Cole was the very first African American to host his own tv show. Now, that’s something. Belting out songs like, “You Send Me” and of course, no one can forget, “Unforgettable”. But, the song that keeps on giving and selling is “The Christmas Song”. Now you may like Mary J. Blige and Johnny Mathis and even Donnie Hathaway. But none can top Ol’ King Cole when it comes to validating the coming of Christmas.  Now for us in Kansas City, we are splitting our time between getting ready for Christmas and getting our Chiefs ready for the playoffs. Baltimore and Miami are like us, waiting for the final word that they are “in the running for the February Super Bowl”. But teams places like Oakland and Tennessee and even Atlanta are singing along, with Nat King Cole and his perennial, “Christmas Song”. That’s all they can sing about, through now. So for us, the song ought to be a reminder that the 10-3 Chiefs are back and have recovered from a dismal last year. Most important, we have proved that Booker and Cantankerous Ike Gardner wrong. They said the Chiefs would not win more than five games this and already they have doubled that. So, I wish they could create a Christmas Song that would memorialize those kind of doubters. Perhaps we could call it, “Wrong Way Ike” and, “Poor, Pitiful Paul”. But thank God for the rest who have/had faith in the Kansas City Chiefs. They can now say proudly that “yes, there is a Santa Claus” and croon along with Nat “King” Cole, at the same time. It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas. Let’s hear from the rest of the guys. Chiefs by 10 Carl Clark: I want K.C. to make the playoffs. Chiefs by 3 Bubba Cleaver: The real 2013 version of the Chiefs are back  Chiefs by 10 Ike Gardner: K.C. will fall in “the Black Hole”. Oakland by 7 Lloyd Greenfield: If the Chiefs play together, they will win. Chiefs by 7 Ollie Hubbard: Raiders leave their hearts in San Francisco. Chiefs by 10 Jim Nunnelly: Santa and the playoffs  are on the way. Chiefs by 17 Ed West: everybody is together, for the rest of the year. Chiefs by 10 Ron Walton: confidence has returned. Chiefs by 7

Monday Nite Footballers Predictions

By Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly

Predicting Since 1970

Kansas City Chiefs vs. Houston Texans

12:00 p.m., KCTV 5

   

   Predictions (Wins In Parenthesis)

Chatter, Conversation And Commentary

 Seven teams have lost their first two games. Unfortunately, one of those teams is our Kansas City Chiefs. What’s more is we are still expecting the Chiefs to be 2-0, like they were this time, last year. Speaking of last year, we were all worried up about Priest Holmes’ hip. You will remember he was not supposed to play at all and he just got well and became the NFL’s top touchdown producer.

 Well, now it’s his knee and ankle. Priest was hurt on a play that bent him backwards and thus, he was held out the remainder of the Carolina game. While Priest’s health is something to talk about, we are still wondering why he was not in the game on the fourth down play, against the Panthers. A guy who is the franchise player. . . who is the

best scorer in the entire league. . . has a burst of speed like no other Chief in history (except Mike Garrett). . . and Vermeil chose to go to a second stringer. Hmmmmm. Five days later, and there still is no reasonable explanation why Priest was not in the game. Maybe there was another injury or just plain bad coaching.

 Speaking of injuries, the wide receiver corps is affected again. Kennison and Morton are probable for this week. That means they will play. Who is their right mind would not play Kennison, the only deep threat the Chiefs have? Look for (Kennison) to lead the Chiefs to their first victory, this Sunday out at Arrowhead.

They played half-way respectably against the Colts. The defense has developed and for the most part, they “hung  in there”. But the Chiefs’ problems are far beyond the struggling offensive line and the newly-appointed quarterback. It goes much deeper than that. Either the Chiefs are the "best of the worst" or they are “the worst of the best”. Either way, they have failed to convince anyone that they are serious contenders. Just reflect on how the national sportscasters ignore us completely, preferring to show highlights of our opponents. That alone tells you that no one thinks the Chiefs are important enough to even mention. At 4-6, we will again struggle in December to make it to a .500 season. And you will remember that we really didn’t make the playoffs last year. Through a series of luck, we fortuitously landed into the playoffs, only to be ousted quickly. And so let’s start thinking about 2008. Or if you are not ready for that, let’s start looking to who will represent the AFC in the Super Bowl. Will it be undefeated New England or badly-shaken Indianapolis? And start looking at Dallas and Green Bay. Now those are complete teams, combining defense and offense and special teams. Perhaps the Chiefs ought to relinquish all their games and instead, allow these teams to mentor them in the art of winning. If they do that, maybe they will grow and mature into a respectable NFL franchise. &hTab;  So, as the holiday season starts, relieve yourself of any fancy thoughts about the Chiefs. Instead, transfer your loyalty to one of the real teams. That way, you will have a great Thanksgiving. Something the Chiefs cannot give you, this year.

frames.text: The Hubbards, Opinions,  And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: The Hubbards, Opinions,
And The Chiefs

frames.text: The Monday Niters are full of themselves. They freely share their opinions and don’t care if  anyone agrees with them or not. And we’ll share some of those community-related opinions, right after we comment about the Hubbard family and their cooking talents. This last Monday night was their time to host the Monday Niters. As usual, there was a feast. African cabbage, red beans and rice, chicken wings, catfish, spaghetti, green beans and potatoes, cole slaw, cornbread and rolls. Even their lovely daughter, Kim, dropped by to taste the Hubbard Buffet, But, there was something different tis week. Usually, Ollie does all the cooking. But this time, it was his sassy wife, Sandra, who  did it all. Yes, Sandra. Now, she is no stranger to the culinary arts. Her late mother was truly a great cook. In fact, in Macon, Missouri, Mrs. McElroy was a well-known caterer throughout north central Missouri. Now, if you don’t know where Macon is. It near Clarence, Missouri. Don’t know where that is. It’s near LaPlata, Still don’t know? Forget it. Neither do most people. But Sandra was the only black child in the school band. And she was the first black child born in the Macon County hospital. And she spent most of her days, living and thriving in an all-white world. But if you tasted her buffet on Monday, one would know she is truly an African American artist, when it comes to cooking. Even Ike Gardner, the most opinionated African American alive, liked the red beans and rice. So did Ed West, who went back several times. But husband Ollie was present and offered his supervision to the whole process. Bottom line, the Hubbards did their thing, especially on Monday night. . . sharing their  cooking talents  and opinions.  Let’s start with Ollie and see what he and the other Monday Niters are thinking, about community events and the Chiefs. Ollie Hubbard: Ollie is concerned about how all this violence is affecting our children. So, he is urging each of us to make sure our children stay in school for their own safety. But he is no longer concerned about the Chiefs. He says the Chiefs will kick the Giants’ butt, on Sunday. Chiefs by 10. Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still concerned about Alzheimer’s disease. In fact, he says that the toll is not only on the patients but on the care-givers, as well. Caregivers often think the patient may get better and deny the reality of getting worse. But he thinks the Chiefs are “not in denial”. He says Sunday will be a “Giant killer day” for the 3-0 Chiefs. Chiefs by 14. Paul Booker: He thinks the city leaders are on the right track, by inviting leaders from other cities to discuss the crime problem. Recent visitors from Chicago are helping us address this violence thing. He feels the same way about the Chiefs’ defense. They will slaughter Eli Manning on Sunday. Chiefs by 3. Carl Clark: He believes that the sentencing ought to fit the crime. Bad crime, long time in jail. Just that simple. Feeling the same way about the Chiefs. They will be criminal, against New York. Giants by 14. Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver: Cleaver just finished his favorite week in Washington, hosting the Legislative Black Caucus. Only a few know how significant he is in Washington. Everybody knows and respects Emanuel Cleaver. And he knows the Chiefs will be like David and slaughter the Goliaths. Chiefs by 10. Ike “Mad Man” Gardner: Ike is concerned about the lack of jobs. He feels that jobs are the crux of our social structure. Known for freely expressing his opinion. Ike is right about the jobs but wrong about the game on Sunday at Arrowhead. He thinks the Chiefs’ fairy tale is over. Giants by 7. Lloyd Greenfield: He believes that to be educated is the key to a successful life. And that we must not let education get lost in all the violence discussions. Like with the Chiefs, we must “keep on keeping on”. Chiefs by 3. Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He is still reeling over the central city representation at the recent Mental Health speak-out. One-third of the participants were African American and they came through like champs, offering their insightful opinions freely. Congratulations to each of you that attended. Now, let’s not allow the Chiefs to get depressed again. Jamaal Charles and the defense will stop that from happening. Chiefs by 7 Ed West: He still harping on the police control thing. Plainly, the control of the police department should be left alone. Period. And look to the Chiefs defense (Poe, Hali and Houston)  to shut Eli down. Chiefs by 10.

Everybody knows and respects Emanuel Cleaver. And he knows the Chiefs will be like David and slaughter the Goliaths. Chiefs by 10.

Lloyd Greenfield: He believes that to be educated is the key to a successful life. And that we must not let education get lost in all the violence discussions. Like with the Chiefs, we must “keep on keeping on”. Chiefs by 3.

Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He is still reeling over the central city representation at the recent Mental Health speak-out. One-third of the participants were African American and they came through like champs, offering their insightful opinions freely. Congratulations to each of you that attended. Now, let’s not allow the Chiefs to get depressed again. Jamaal Charles and the defense will stop that from happening. Chiefs by 7

Ed West: He still harping on the police control thing. Plainly, the control of the police department should be left alone. Period. And look to the Chiefs defense (Poe, Hali and Houston)  to shut Eli down. Chiefs by 10.

frames.text: You all will remember George Benson, a jazz singer-guitarist, who crooned his way into our memories with a song called, “Masquerade”.  The song was about a couple of lovers, who were “masking” their activities, which led to the question about a “masquerade”.  Well, the Chiefs are 4-2 now and many still think the Chiefs are not who we think they are. And this week will be a real test to see if the Chiefs are really “just masquerading”.  Hmmmm! And like always, we Monday Niters are wondering if the Chiefs are really contenders for the playoffs or are they just “pretenders”.   First, they are us loyalists, who believe in the Chiefs, thick or thin, lose or win. We see hope in the making and like Obama used to say...yes, we can.  And then there are the “haters”, who despite some real evidence, still cling to the notion that the Chiefs will fade soon.  But, one “big hater” changed his vote this week. So, let’s inquire with each Monday Niter and query if the Chiefs will be playing beyond January 2. Dr. Charles “The Chef” Allen:  Doc quit a good job at Bendix to pursue his life-long dream of becoming a dentist.  That he did and for thirty two years now, he has delivered “pain free” dentistry to this community.   So as the “main loyalist”, Doc sees the Chiefs undoubtedly making the playoffs. He finds great hope in the “B Boys”. He believes that Bowe and Berry are exactly what the “doc” ordered, on offense and defense respectively, No mask here. Chiefs by 10 Paul “Hater No. 1” Booker:  When Paul was an educator and a home-school coordinator for the District, he was kind, effective and knowledgeable.  Being from the Bootheel, he appeared that he was happy, go-lucky.  But, Paul was forced to pick cotton down in Haiti, Mo.  And he carries that “hate” with him, right onto things like the Chiefs.  No matter what the Chiefs do, Paul just says “no” to the Chiefs.  He says the same about their playoff chances. And about the Chiefs against winless Buffalo.  A real “hater”.  Take off your mask, Booker...it is a brand new day, Buffalo by 7. Carl “Car Crazy” Clark: You want to see Carl light up?  Just ask him about his beloved, 1987 Corvette. He longs for that speed, that body, and that low center of gravity, But when asked about the Chiefs’ playoff chances, he is not as forward as Doc, nor as difficult as “that Booker”.  He recognizes some improvement but knows the Chiefs have not really been tested and have lost to the good teams, like Indianapolis and Houston.  So we might have to restore his Corvette to get him to say “yes” but for now, he is moving in the right direction. Chiefs by 3. Congressman “Still Got It” Cleaver:  His wife, Dianne, took him to dinner, last Tuesday.  It was his birthday and despite a tedious campaign for re-election, he went and had fun. But the real fun will come on October 30 when the whole community is invited to help him celebrate his birthday, at Ararat Temple.   Evelyn Champagne King and the Bloodstones will be there to sing “happy birthday”, even though he is still wearing a mask about his real age.  But, on Sunday, he thinks the Chiefs will beat Buffalo and further enhance their chances of playing beyond the regular season. Happy Birthday Rev and everyone will be there, with voter registration cards and five dollars. By the way, Ararat Temple is just north of the Peachtree Buffet. It all starts at 8. Chiefs by 10. Ike “The Big Hater” Gardner:  Ike was once the chairman of the Desegregation Task Force, some 40 or so years ago.  And as an educator and a parent, he knew a lot about the “ins and outs” of the School District.  And when he is talking about that part of his life, he is kind, considerate and engaging.  However, he has grown to become a “hater of everything”.   Speak of the Chiefs and he will immediately inform you about the coaching “mental midgets”, referring to Haley and Weis. And this week, he has returned to his old, School District self.  He actually is predicting that the Chiefs, though still spotty, will beat Buffalo. POW! Did you get that, George Benson? Chiefs by 3 Lloyd “The Biker” Greenfield:   Lloyd owns a motorcycle. Not just any big bike.  It’s a Harley Davidson Soft Tail Heritage Motorcycle.  Now, that’s class. He once rode all the way to Houston, Texas on his toy, He still can be seen around town with his fellow Buffalo Soldiers, Peter Yelorda and Marques Harris.  While just cruising, Lloyd has often reflected on the Chiefs and how they have adopted some winning ways, slowly jelling into a playoff team.  There ain’t do doubt that the Chiefs will be going to the playoffs, starting Sunday out at Arrowhead.  Biking but betting on the locals. Chiefs by 6.   Ollie “Meet The Press” Hubbard:  Whenever you talk to Ollie, you feel like you are talking to the press.  You have to be real careful what you tell him because he is GONNA report it. But, all of us can attest to his helpful hospitality.  He will help you out, no matter what.  There ain’t no wearing a mask with Ollie.   He is who he is and we all accept and admire him for that.  In fact, Ollie has been the same, ever since he was a little boy, running in and out of his father’s barber shop, down on 18th Street.  That’s probably where his “inquiring mind” began.   But, Ollie knows that the Chiefs are back, just like he is with his ability to get around.  No doubt about it, Chiefs are contenders and he is going to tell everybody.  What’s new? Chiefs by 10. Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly:  Came to town the same year the Chiefs qualified for the Super Bowl in 1969.   And after retiring from Jackson County, has returned to the health care industry, helping especially with Health Care Reform.  But, he remembers the glory days of the Chiefs.  Those like Otis Taylor and Buck Buchanan and Emmitt Thomas roamed our streets, patronized our businesses and attended our churches. He yearns for the return to the good old days when the Rodgers Health center and Swope Health Services were born. There was no masquerading then for everyone had jobs and businesses were booming, up and down Troost and around 31st  street. That is when he met and became friends with all these Monday Niters.   He believes that the Chiefs are not “lost in a masquerade” and are rising again and will definitely make the playoffs. Chiefs by 22. Ed “Mr. I-Phone” West: While the rest of us struggle with modern technology, Ed West welcomes it.  If a question about anything comes up, Ed just whispers into his i-phone and reads the answer.  Now, he does wish the i-phone had big print because he has to wear them triple-bi-focal glasses.  Nonetheless, he is a very valuable resource to our community.   Besides technology, Ed is actively engaged in helping teenagers adjust to the Raytown School District.  And while he is by far the most factual Monday Niter, he is by no means swayed by the invading “haters”.  He thinks the Chiefs are growing by “leaps and bounds” and will definitely win the AFC West. And he is not wearing a mask, at all.  Chiefs by 20.

frames.text: Despite the ill wishes of the diehard “Manning maniacs”, the New Orleans Saints did go marching in..they crucified the Colts, this past Sunday at the Super Bowl.  In fact, it is hard to find anyone who was “for” the Colts, after that second display of  second half redemption. No one will ever forget the score at the end of the first half...neither will we ever forget the going for the Saints’ gutsy playcalling, even though they failed to score...and no one will forget the on-side kick that split the “Red Sea” for the Saints...and God Almighty blessed little Tracy Porter with a “Manning bullet” and the rest is history.  Good going Saints....you made it all worth watching.  Now back to those who predicted the games.  Here are the Saints and here are the Ponies.  THOSE WHO THOUGHT THE SAINTS WOULD WIN!  Vicki Frazier, Renee Gardner, Breana Jordan, Montoya Lucas, Kosha Johnson, Danielle Morris, Rich McCauley, Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly, Erica Nunnelly, Jazel Nunnelly, Christian Nunnelly, Gerald Pegg, LaMetria Pegg, Margo Quiriconi, Eric L. Wesson, Arionne Williams and Patricia Wright. THOSE WHO NEW THE SAINTS WOULD WIN! Eric L. Wesson  THOSE WHO  MISTAKENLY  PICKED THE COLTS  TO WIN! Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, CB Cadenhead, Carl Clark,Congressman Cleaver, Dyan Deveraux, Charles Fort (San Diego), Ike “Papaw” Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield, Ollie Hubbard, Clyde McQueen (Full Employment Council), Donna Stewart, and Ed West,  FINAL WORDS!  We will not remind you that it has been a long time coming for the Saints.  Just about the same time it has been since the Chiefs have been to the Super Bowl.  Every team in the AFC West has been since we last went in 1970.  Let’s hope and pray our Chiefs make the right draft choices and make it easier for Kansas City to compete.  And of course, we, Monday Niters along with THE CALL, are doing our part to get Otis Taylor into the NFL Hall Of Fame....now that would be something....and to the Colts’ fans...maybe next year.  For now, the rest of us will gloat over the fact that WE were in “that number”....when the Saints went marching in....

frames.text: African Cabbage, Mrs. Myla Banks, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: African Cabbage, Mrs. Myla Banks, And The Chiefs

frames.text: We, Monday Niters, know that when we go to Dr. Allen’s house, there will be “something new”. Of course, Dr. Allen, a long-respected dentist, fashions himself as a culinary artist. He thrives on finding different foods to serve us.  This week it was African cabbage, merlot-induced gravy, a medley of beans, macaroni with ham and peas, fried chicken strips and Yorkshire pig feet. Yes, we had pig feet and it was presented as a delightful delicacy.  Of course, Dr. Allen recognized the essential contributions of his daughter, Tee and his wife, Beverly. Commonly called the “A Team”, they helped us celebrate the Chiefs’ victory over Green Bay.  It certainly helped that Dr. Allen was the only Monday Niter to pick the Chiefs over Green Bay. So he was all smiles. Even overly-mean Ike Gardner was grinning. That’s because Mrs. Myla Banks, a long-time educator in the Kansas City Missouri School District, actually phoned Ike. That shows you how nice Mrs. Banks is because no one calls Ike just to chat. Right there in the middle of the game, he and Mrs. Banks talked about old times and she chided Ike for being so hard on the Chiefs. In fact, she flat-out told him she was picking the Chiefs over Oakland, Saturday at Arrowhead. Of course, everyone saluted Mrs. Banks because she has been one of our most faithful readers of our column. That’s a blessing because Mrs. Banks still can be seen around town, talking to the owner of the Chiefs or conversing at the annual NAACP luncheon.  Thanks, Mrs. Banks, but that wasn’t all that happened. Paul “Hater of All Haters” Booker actually made a confession, stopping all the usual noise. And you will have to read his comments below to find out exactly what he said to “blow us all away”. We were floored and most of us went home, knowing that Booker had been “touched” by something. The 19-14 victory over Green Bay must have surprised him big-time. And so it was with the Chiefs. The Chiefs could not believe it, themselves. Green Bay came to town, undefeated and expected to just beat up the lowly-Chiefs and move on toward the Super Bowl. But, Tambi Hali and the defense gave the offense some room. And the new quarterback, Orton, looked like he “done found him a job”. When was the last time you saw a Chiefs’ quarterback zip a pass between two defenders? Face it, Orton is the “O” factor and should be expected to help the Chiefs this week. And if things work out against Oakland, then the new Chiefs with the “O’ factor will return to Denver, against the team that cut him four weeks ago. Speaking of Oakland, will the Chiefs make a serious run for the playoffs? Let’s see what the Monday Niters think. Now, be sure to look for what Booker said. Dr. Charles Allen: The new coach, Romeo Crennel, has created a new culture in the Chiefs’ organization. That culture led to a big, unexpected showing against Green Bay. The formidable Packers were not looking for a tough game against the Chiefs. But the Chiefs came through, just like Charles said they would. Chiefs by 10 Paul “the Converted Apostle” Booker: Booker says the change in attitude among the players is remarkable. They just wouldn’t play for Todd the Tyrant. MERRY CHRISTMAS FROM THE MONDAY NITERS. . . Although the Kansas City Chiefs won’t be participating in the 2004 NFL playoffs, the Monday Niters still want to wish its readers and Kansas City a Merry Christmas and a Happy New Year. Shown are, Paul Booker, Charles Allen, Jim Nunnelly, Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield, and Carl Clark. Not shown are Bubba Cleaver, Ollie Hubbard and Ed West. -- CALL photo by Rex Purefoy

Charles Allen Chiefs by 14 Repeat performance

Paul Booker Chiefs by 10 Larry fell down but he got up

Carl Clark Chiefs by 7 Chiefs will plug up the Black Hole

Bubba Cleaver Chiefs by 14 Battle of the used-to-be’s; but we be's      better

Ike Gardner Chiefs by 1 Stevie Wonder fights Ray Charles

Lloyd   Chiefs by 7 And the beat(ing) goes on!

Greenfield 

Ollie Hubbard  Raiders by 6  Raiders will walk the plank again

Jim Nunnelly Chiefs by 23 Johnson saves Vermeil's -- (job)

Ed West  Raiders by 20 Reverse psychology, still in effect

Chatter, Conversation And Commentary

 When high-powered, highly-paid coaches sign on to become a head coach in the NFL,

there are lots of neat little “perks” that find their way into a contract.

 For example, there are additional dollars added, when a team makes the playoffs or avoid a losing season. Well, for the Chiefs, Vermeil and company will not be in the hunt

for the playoffs. But, if they win the next two games, that could mean “bigger bucks”

for the coaches. For while they would not have had a winning season, it would not be

a losing season, either.

 This is just a lesson in the “small print” of these big-time contracts. Then, too, Vermeil has some making up to do both with the fans and specifically, with Larry Johnson. This boy can run that ball, equal to or better than Priest Holmes. And Vermeil, because of some personal issues with Johnson, kept Johnson out of competition, even though he was a high-round, draft choice. And to see Johnson perform like he has lately, Vermeil has to save face and let Larry run around, through, and over Oakland. Look for Larry and the Chiefs to save Dick Vermeil’s -- (job). More important, a full stadium on Christmas Day will help save any threatened decrease in season ticket sales. On the other hand, the Chiefs should not expect the fans to pay for an increase in ticket prices. For really, this season has been mediocre, at best. Chiefs 40, Raiders 17.

 Note: Congressman-elect Cleaver is still homeless in D.C., having failed to locate an apartment on his last trip East. Ike Gardner and Ed West, fellow Monday Niters and St. James members, are assisting Cleaver by providing contacts. Cleaver is planning to be in Washington Tuesday thru Thursday of every week and here in Kansas City Friday through Monday. Cleaver will return to Washington for swearing-in ceremonies on January 4, 2005, At that time, he hopes to surrender his homelessness card.

paragraphs.text: Hank Stram, Enlarging Our Territory

frames.text: &hTab;Hank Stram was the first head coach of the Kansas City Chiefs. &hTab;Only those of us over 50 will remember the days when Kansas City was part of the old American Football League. This was the early sixties, when the predominant National Football League touted franchises. . . like the Chicago Bears, San Francisco Forty-Niners, and the Washington Redskins. And Hank Stram and others had the task of competing with and enlarging the territory of the fragile but willing League. And enlarge they did. And Hank Stram, under the guidance of Lamar Hunt, brought Kansas City up from nowhere into the big leagues. &hTab;Before merging, the AFL actually had to outbid and outwit the more formidable NFL. More important, they also had to outplay them, as well. And that’s where Hank Stram came in. With smaller, lesser-known players, Hank had to be an innovator. With a small, frail quarterback like Len Dawson, Stram implemented a “moving pocket”. That allowed the bigger, faster offensive linemen to outmaneuver the slower, meaner defensive linemen. And that would lead to a more fan-friendly game. &hTab;&hTab;&hTab;While Hank was a master at coaching, he knew how to motivate the newly-found, small-college athletes. Especially the young athletes from Grambling, Southern, and Texas Southern. And it is here where he will be most remembered by folks of color. Never was there any kind of racial uprising or unfair play on any of Stram’s teams. He just didn’t tolerate it and he made everybody feel included. More important, he treated them fairly at the pocketbook level, as well. Many came poor and left well-paid, especially in their later years. In conclusion, Hank Stram was more than innovation to this new-f league. He was more than a coach, who coined phrases like “matriculating down the field”.  Since Stram was in charge, we have not been near a Super Bowl. But he was right up there with Branch Rickey, who cleared the path for Jackie Robinson to play major league baseball. With the same level of commitment, Stram cleared the “economic path” for these young unheard-of athletes, to make a lot of money. Simple as that. He did enlarge our territory. &hTab;Thanks, Hank.

frames.text: Kansas City Chiefs vs. Denver Broncos 7:30 p.m., ESPN and Channel 9 &hTab; &hTab; Predictions Chatter, Conversation And Commentary Isn’t it funny that we are all worried about the Chiefs’ defense? It wasn’t that long ago when we were all equally concerned about the Chiefs’ offense.  So it goes. The vicissitudes of professional football are what makes for the continued, record-breaking popularity of the game.  And it will all start this Sunday, with the Chiefs visiting arch-rival, the Denver Broncos. Our readers will remember that the Chiefs actually won 13 regular-season games last year (the best in the National Football League).  While some of the games could have gone either way, the Chiefs generally rose to the last-minute occasion.  That is a good thing. With Boerigter out for the season and Johnnie Morton crippled, all of a sudden, everyone is talking about how the Chiefs are lacking in receivers.  Do not sweat it!  The Chiefs were overstocked in receivers last year, anyway.  Remember, how much Tony Gonzalez used to complain about his few touches.  And don’t forget about Eddie Kenniston, who I believe to be the “best” Chiefs’ receiver.  And Dante Hall will be all right, since every special teams coach will be geared to limit his return yardage. Denver will pose a tough test, especially for our defense.  But, most of us think the Chiefs’ offense will prevail, especially with the stable of running backs, featuring Larry Johnson and Priest Holmes. &hTab;Look for the Chiefs to win, by a narrow margin.
